# lru - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lru/

## Expand description

An implementation of a LRU cache. The cache supports `get`, `get_mut`, `put`,
and `pop` operations, all of which are O(1). This crate was heavily influenced
by the [LRU Cache implementation in an earlier version of Rust’s std::collections crate](https://doc.rust-lang.org/0.12.0/std/collections/lru_cache/struct.LruCache.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
extern crate lru;
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
fn main() {
        let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
        cache.put("apple", 3);
        cache.put("banana", 2);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"apple").unwrap(), 3);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 2);
        assert!(cache.get(&"pear").is_none());
        assert_eq!(cache.put("banana", 4), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(cache.put("pear", 5), None);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"pear").unwrap(), 5);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 4);
        assert!(cache.get(&"apple").is_none());
        {
            let v = cache.get_mut(&"banana").unwrap();
            *v = 6;
        }
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 6);
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Into](https://docs.rs/struct.IntoIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator that moves out of a `LruCache`.
- [Iter](https://docs.rs/struct.Iter.html)
- An iterator over the entries of a `LruCache`.
- [IterMut](https://docs.rs/struct.IterMut.html)
- An iterator over mutables entries of a `LruCache`.
- [LruCache](https://docs.rs/struct.LruCache.html)
- An LRU Cache

# lru 0.18.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/lru/latest

# LRU Cache

An implementation of a LRU cache. The cache supports `put`, `get`, `get_mut` and `pop` operations,
all of which are O(1). This crate was heavily influenced by the [LRU Cache implementation in an
earlier version of Rust's std::collections crate](https://doc.rust-lang.org/0.12.0/std/collections/lru_cache/struct.LruCache.html).

The MSRV for this crate is 1.85.0.

## Example

Below is a simple example of how to instantiate and use a LRU cache.

```
extern crate lru;
use LruCache;
use NonZeroUsize;
```

# hashbrown - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hashbrown/^0.17.0/

## Expand description

This crate is a Rust port of Google’s high-performance [SwissTable](https://abseil.io/blog/20180927-swisstables) hash
map, adapted to make it a drop-in replacement for Rust’s standard `HashMap`
and `HashSet` types.

The original C++ version of [SwissTable](https://abseil.io/blog/20180927-swisstables) can be found [here](https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp/blob/master/absl/container/internal/raw_hash_set.h), and this
[CppCon talk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ncHmEUmJZf4) gives an overview of how the algorithm works.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [hash_](https://docs.rs/hash_map/index.html)- map
- A hash map implemented with quadratic probing and SIMD lookup.
- [hash_](https://docs.rs/hash_set/index.html)- set
- A hash set implemented as a `HashMap`where the value is`()`.
- [hash_](https://docs.rs/hash_table/index.html)- table
- A hash table implemented with quadratic probing and SIMD lookup.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Default](https://docs.rs/struct.DefaultHashBuilder.html)- Hash - Builder
- Default hash builder for the `S`type parameter of`HashMap``HashSet`
- [Default](https://docs.rs/struct.DefaultHasher.html)- Hasher
- Default hasher for `HashMap``HashSet`
- [HashMap](https://docs.rs/struct.HashMap.html)
- A hash map implemented with quadratic probing and SIMD lookup.
- [HashSet](https://docs.rs/struct.HashSet.html)
- A hash set implemented as a `HashMap`where the value is`()`.
- [Hash](https://docs.rs/struct.HashTable.html)- Table
- Low-level hash table with explicit hashing.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [TryReserve](https://docs.rs/enum.TryReserveError.html)- Error
- The error type for `try_reserve`methods.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Equivalent](https://docs.rs/trait.Equivalent.html)
- Key equivalence trait.

# scoped_threadpool - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scoped_threadpool/0.1.*/

## Expand description

This crate provides a stable, safe and scoped threadpool.

It can be used to execute a number of short-lived jobs in parallel without the need to respawn the underlying threads.

Jobs are runnable by borrowing the pool for a given scope, during which
an arbitrary number of them can be executed. These jobs can access data of
any lifetime outside of the pools scope, which allows working on
non-`'static` references in parallel.

For safety reasons, a panic inside a worker thread will not be isolated, but rather propagate to the outside of the pool.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples:

```
extern crate scoped_threadpool;
use scoped_threadpool::Pool;
fn main() {
    // Create a threadpool holding 4 threads
    let mut pool = Pool::new(4);
    let mut vec = vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
    // Use the threads as scoped threads that can
    // reference anything outside this closure
    pool.scoped(|scope| {
        // Create references to each element in the vector ...
        for e in &mut vec {
            // ... and add 1 to it in a seperate thread
            scope.execute(move || {
                *e += 1;
            });
        }
    });
    assert_eq!(vec, vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]);
}
```

# stats_alloc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/stats_alloc/0.1.*/

## Expand description

An instrumenting middleware for global allocators in Rust, useful in testing for validating assumptions regarding allocation patterns, and potentially in production loads to monitor for memory leaks.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
extern crate stats_alloc;
use stats_alloc::{Region, StatsAlloc, INSTRUMENTED_SYSTEM};
use std::alloc::System;
#[global_allocator]
static GLOBAL: &StatsAlloc<System> = &INSTRUMENTED_SYSTEM;
fn main() {
    let reg = Region::new(&GLOBAL);
    let x: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(1_024);
    println!("Stats at 1: {:#?}", reg.change());
    // Used here to ensure that the value is not
    // dropped before we check the statistics
    ::std::mem::size_of_val(&x);
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Region](https://docs.rs/struct.Region.html)
- A snapshot of the allocation statistics, which can be used to determine
allocation changes while the `Region`is alive.
- [Stats](https://docs.rs/struct.Stats.html)
- Allocator statistics
- [Stats](https://docs.rs/struct.StatsAlloc.html)- Alloc
- An instrumenting middleware which keeps track of allocation, deallocation, and reallocation requests to the underlying global allocator.

## Statics[§](https://docs.rs#statics)

- [INSTRUMENTED_](https://docs.rs/static.INSTRUMENTED_SYSTEM.html)- SYSTEM
- An instrumented instance of the system allocator.

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# overseerd-client 0.9.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/overseerd-client/0.9.0

The Overseerd protocol-agnostic client *contract*.

The framework implements no client calls. It defines **capabilities** a protocol may
support — one trait each — and a protocol (`overseerd-rpc`, a future HTTP binding, …)
implements the subset it can. A protocol *declares* support by implementing a capability
and *refuses* by simply not: a client-streaming call over HTTP/1.1 is then a compile
error — a protocol limitation expressed in the type system, never a framework limit.

| Capability | trait | HTTP/1.1 | HTTP/2 | gRPC | custom RPC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| one req → one resp | [ `Unary`] | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| one req → many resp | [ `ServerStreaming`] | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| many req → one resp | [ `ClientStreaming`] | — | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| many req ↔ many resp | [ `BidiStreaming`] | — | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

The protocol owns **everything** behind each method: body encoding and parsing, framing,
routing, and streaming. A streaming capability returns the protocol's own response
[`Stream`] as an associated type — a real contract that the result *is* a stream of
decoded items, not an opaque box that would pretend any stream fits.

A generated client (`FooClient<C>`) bounds `C` on exactly the capabilities its RPCs need
and delegates to them, so the same generated code runs over any protocol providing those
capabilities.

The framework assumes **no serialization**: it never bounds a message on `serde` (a
protocol might use rkyv, protobuf, …). Instead a protocol declares what it can carry by
implementing [`Encodes<T>`] / [`Decodes<T>`] for those message types (typically a blanket
`impl<T: Serialize> Encodes<T>`, or `impl<T: Archive> Encodes<T>`, …). A capability method
is bound `where Self: Encodes<Req> + Decodes<Resp>`, so a message the protocol cannot
serialize is a compile error — protocol-defined, never framework-assumed.

Pipeline: source → [ lexer](https://docs.rs/lexer/index.html) →

[→](https://docs.rs/parser/index.html)

`parser`[→ [](https://docs.rs/ast/index.html)

`ast``eval`] → placed

`ir`[, later PNG/PDF). This crate is pure (no file I/O); the CLI and WASM wrappers drive it.](https://docs.rs/svg/index.html)

- Compile pic source into a placed-primitive `Drawing`
- [compile_](https://docs.rs/fn.compile_in_dir.html)- in_ - dir
- Compile pic source, resolving `copy "file"`includes relative to`base`.
- [compile_](https://docs.rs/fn.compile_json.html)- json
- Compile to a single JSON object `{ "svg": "...", "animations": [...], "diagnostics": [...] }`, or`{ "error": "..." }`on failure. This is the entry point the WASM wrapper and browser playground consume.
- [diagnostics_](https://docs.rs/fn.diagnostics_json.html)- json
- Build the JSON diagnostic array emitted by pic `print`statements.
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_svg.html)- svg
- Compile pic source directly to an SVG string.
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_svg_in_dir.html)- svg_ - in_ - dir
- Render pic source to SVG, resolving `copy "file"`includes relative to`base`.
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_math_renderer.html)- math_ - renderer
- Register the process-wide math renderer. The first call wins; later calls are ignored (returns whether this call installed the renderer).

# mockforge_vbr - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/mockforge-vbr/0.3.198/mockforge_vbr/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#mockforge-virtual-backend-reality-vbr-engine)MockForge Virtual Backend Reality (VBR) Engine

The VBR engine creates stateful mock servers with persistent virtual databases, auto-generated CRUD APIs, relationship constraints, session management, and time-based data evolution.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

VBR acts like a mini real backend with:

- Persistent virtual database (SQLite, JSON, in-memory options)
- CRUD APIs auto-generated from entity schemas
- Relationship modeling and constraint enforcement
- User session & auth emulation
- Time-based data evolution (data aging, expiring sessions)

[§](https://docs.rs#example-usage)Example Usage

```
use mockforge_vbr::{VbrEngine, VbrConfig};
let config = VbrConfig::default()
    .with_storage_backend(mockforge_vbr::StorageBackend::Sqlite {
        path: "./data/vbr.db".into(),
    });
let engine = VbrEngine::new(config).await?;
// Define entities and generate living API
```

# overseerd_app - Rust

The Overseerd protocol-agnostic application core.

This crate ties the DI engine, config, hooks, and dirs into a runnable [ App](https://docs.rs/app/struct.App.html) that is

[it installs. It owns the](https://docs.rs/protocol/trait.ProtocolPlugin.html)

# overseerd_axum_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd-axum-macros/0.9.0/overseerd_axum_macros/

## Expand description

The Overseerd **axum/HTTP controller** macros: `#[controller]`, `#[handlers]`, and the
route attributes (`#[get]`, `#[post]`, `#[put]`, `#[delete]`, `#[patch]`, `#[head]`,
`#[options]`, and the raw `#[route(METHOD, "/path")]`). They emit `::overseerd::web::*`
types, so they live in their own crate rather than the core `overseerd-macros`, built on
the shared [ overseerd_macros_core](https://docs.rs/overseerd-macros-core/0.9.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/overseerd_macros_core/index.html) codegen.

Re-exported through the `overseerd` facade’s `web` module; depend on the facade, not this
crate directly.

- `#[controller]`is a- **router component**: a- `#[component]`(field-injected singleton) plus a controller header, its- `{Controller}Routes`slice, and its- `ControllerDescriptor`.
- `#[handlers]`is- `MethodArgs<AxumHandlers>`— the base impl macro (- `#[methods]`:- `#[init]`- `#[hook]`) plus the route extension, which registers each route-attributed method.

- The route attributes mark a method inside a `#[handlers]`impl (stripped by`#[handlers]`).

# overseerd_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd-macros/0.9.0/overseerd_macros/

## Expand description

Procedural macros for the Overseerd framework.

These are re-exported from the `overseerd` facade crate; depend on that rather
than this crate directly. They span three subsystems — components (dependency
injection), services (RPC), and configuration.

| Macro | Applies to | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| `#[component]` | struct | `Component`impl + a factory (field-injection default,`factory = path`, or`default_factory = false`for a manual instance) |
| `#[service]` | struct | `Component`+`ServiceComponent`impls + a service header + a factory |
| `#[handlers]` | impl block | RPC handlers + RPC group |
| `#[methods]` | impl block | lifecycle methods — an `#[init]`constructor (an explicit factory) |
| `#[rpc]`/`#[init]` | method | markers consumed by `#[handlers]`/`#[methods]` |
| `#[injectable]` | trait | `Provide<dyn Trait>`impl (under`di-check`) |
| `#[config]` | struct/enum | `ConfigProperties`impl (with field`#[default = ".."]`templated defaults); auto-registers a binding when given`#[config(path = "..")]` |

[§](https://docs.rs#components-two-ways-to-provide-one)Components: two ways to provide one

A *component* is a singleton dependency, resolved by type. There are two ways
to get one into the daemon’s container:

- **System-constructed**— annotate the type with- `#[component]`(or a stateful- `#[service]`). The macro registers a factory; the container builds the instance from its dependencies during startup.
- **Manually provided**— construct the instance yourself and hand it to- `AppBuilder::with_component`. Annotate the type- `#[component(default_factory = false)]`, which emits the- `Component`metadata with no factory.

Both forms register a descriptor in the `DescriptorRegistry`; the difference
is whether the descriptor carries a factory or expects a provided instance.

[§](https://docs.rs#field-injection)Field injection

`#[component]` and `#[service]` build their factory by *field injection*. For
each field of the struct:

- an `Arc<T>`field is treated as a**dependency**and resolved from the container (`cx.resolve::<T>()`);
- a `Cfg<T>`field carrying`#[config("path")]`is a**config binding**resolved by property path (omit the path for the sole-binding shorthand);
- a `#[default]`field is**owned state**, built with`Default::default()`— so its type must implement`Default`, otherwise construct the component another way (an`#[init]`constructor, or`with_component`).

[§](https://docs.rs#implementation)Implementation

Each `#[proc_macro_*]` entry point here is a thin shim: it forwards its token streams to
the matching `expand` function in [ overseerd_macros_core](https://docs.rs/overseerd-macros-core/0.9.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/overseerd_macros_core/index.html), the ordinary library that
holds all the parsing and codegen (a proc-macro crate can only export proc-macros, so the
reusable machinery lives there). Errors are surfaced as

`compile_error!` by the core, not
by panicking.## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [app](https://docs.rs/macro.app.html)
- Assembles an app and validates it from one declaration.
- [daemon](https://docs.rs/macro.daemon.html)- Deprecated
- Deprecated alias for `app!`

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [component](https://docs.rs/attr.component.html)
- Declares a **system-constructed singleton component**on a struct.
- [config](https://docs.rs/attr.config.html)
- Implements the `ConfigProperties`trait for a config`struct`or`enum`, making it injectable as`Cfg<T>`from a property path.
- [injectable](https://docs.rs/attr.injectable.html)
- Marks a trait as injectable as `Arc<dyn Trait>`(providers register with`#[component(provide = dyn Trait)]`).
- [methods](https://docs.rs/attr.methods.html)
- Registers a component’s lifecycle methods from an inherent `impl`block.

# overseerd_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd-config/0.9.0/overseerd_config/

## Expand description

Configuration for the Overseerd framework.

Two layers live here. The **parser** is the format-agnostic core: a normalized
[ ConfigValue](https://docs.rs/enum.ConfigValue.html) tree, a placeholder grammar (

`${KEY}` / `${KEY:default}`), a
[chain, and a custom](https://docs.rs/trait.Resolver.html)

`Resolver`[deserializer that resolves placeholders](https://docs.rs/fn.from_value.html)

`from_value`*while*deserializing. The

**managed**layer (this crate’s

`managed` module) integrates
that parser with dependency injection: [injectables, the](https://docs.rs/struct.Cfg.html)

`Cfg<T>`[that loads and merges files, the](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigManager.html)

`ConfigManager`[resolver the DI container reaches config through, and the two-phase](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigStore.html)

`ConfigStore`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigReloader.html)

`ConfigReloader`The parser’s substitution failure type is [ TemplateError](https://docs.rs/enum.TemplateError.html); the managed layer’s
load/bind failure type is

[.](https://docs.rs/enum.ConfigError.html)

`ConfigError`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigManager.html)- Manager

- The config-reload hook kind: a `#[hook(ConfigReload)]`method runs when a config it targets is reloaded, receiving the proposed value(s) as`CfgNext<T>``HookOutcome`

- [Resolver](https://docs.rs/struct.ResolverChain.html)- Chain

# overseerd_macros_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd-macros-core/0.9.0/overseerd_macros_core/

## Expand description

Shared codegen library for the Overseerd proc-macros.

A proc-macro crate can only export proc-macros, so the reusable codegen lives here as an ordinary library that the macro crates build on:

- **Core macros**—- `#[component]`,- `#[config]`,- `#[methods]`,- `#[injectable]`— are expanded here and surfaced by- `overseerd-macros`
- **Building blocks**— attribute parsing (- `attr`- `extend`- `paths`- `inject`- `hook`- `di`- `provide`- `handle`- `methods`]) — are- **public**, so a plugin’s macro crate (e.g.- `overseerd-rpc-macros`) reuses them to build its own macros (- `#[service]`,- `#[handlers]`, …) without forking the codegen.

# awsm_renderer_materials - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/awsm-renderer-materials/0.13.0/awsm_renderer_materials/

## Expand description

Pluggable material shaders for the `awsm-renderer` visibility-buffer pipeline.

See `README.md` for a high-level overview, the trait contract, and the
rationale for the askama-substitution mechanism.

Each material is a Cargo feature in this crate (`pbr-standard`, `unlit`,
`toon`). The `MaterialShader` trait is the contract every shading model
satisfies. `awsm-renderer` walks the enabled set as a registry to generate
the dispatch table and concatenate WGSL fragments at shader-template time.

- [shader_](https://docs.rs/shader_id/index.html)- id
- Material shader identifiers.
- [shader_](https://docs.rs/shader_includes/index.html)- includes
- Per-material declaration of which shared shader modules and pre-shade fragment inputs a shading model needs — the heart of “skinny materials”.
- [texture](https://docs.rs/texture/index.html)
- Texture reference used by materials.
- [texture_](https://docs.rs/texture_context/index.html)- context
- Abstraction over the renderer’s texture pool / sampler set for material uniform-buffer writers.
- [toon](https://docs.rs/toon/index.html)
- Toon material — banded diffuse + stepped Blinn-Phong specular + rim.
- [unlit](https://docs.rs/unlit/index.html)
- Unlit material — constant emissive surface, no lighting.
- [writer](https://docs.rs/writer/index.html)
- Helpers for packing material parameters into the GPU storage buffer
`awsm-renderer`dispatches against.

# overseerd_dirs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd-dirs/0.9.0/overseerd_dirs/

## Expand description

Unified application directories, injectable as `Dir<K>`.

A [ DirectoriesManager](https://docs.rs/struct.DirectoriesManager.html) (built from project metadata, typically in

`main`)
resolves the platform’s per-application directories — config, data, cache, state,
runtime, and temp — via the `directories` crate’s XDG / Known-Folder logic. Each
is handed out as a typed [keyed by a marker (](https://docs.rs/struct.Dir.html)

`Dir<K>`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Config.html)

`Config`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Runtime.html)

`Runtime`[, …), so a component injects exactly the directory it needs:](https://docs.rs/struct.Tmp.html)

`Tmp`The manager’s directory list is consumed by the config crate (to resolve `${@runtime}`
and friends) and seeded into the daemon, so directory resolution is defined once. This
crate is standalone — it depends only on `overseerd-core` and `overseerd-di`, and knows
nothing about config.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Cache](https://docs.rs/struct.Cache.html)
- Discardable cached data.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.Config.html)
- Configuration files (`application.toml`, …).
- [Data](https://docs.rs/struct.Data.html)
- Persistent application data.
- [Dir](https://docs.rs/struct.Dir.html)
- A resolved application directory of kind `K`, injectable by value.
- [Directories](https://docs.rs/struct.DirectoriesManager.html)- Manager
- Resolves and hands out the application’s `Dir<K>`
- [Runtime](https://docs.rs/struct.Runtime.html)
- Runtime files (sockets, pid files); falls back to the cache dir.
- [State](https://docs.rs/struct.State.html)
- State that should persist but is not user data (logs, history).
- [Tmp](https://docs.rs/struct.Tmp.html)
- The system temporary directory (shared, not app-scoped).

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [DirKind](https://docs.rs/trait.DirKind.html)
- A kind of application directory. Implemented by the marker types and used by
`DirectoriesManager``Dir<Self>`

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_GPU_BUFFER_BYTES.html)- GPU_ - BUFFER_ - BYTES
- Always-on hard ceiling for a single GPU buffer allocation. A request at or
above this is rejected as a recoverable `Err`*before*it reaches the WebGPU API, instead of being passed through to abort the whole renderer process.
- [OVERSIZED_](https://docs.rs/constant.OVERSIZED_ALLOC_BYTES.html)- ALLOC_ - BYTES
- Soft diagnostic threshold: any single GPU allocation larger than this is
flagged as a likely runaway size computation (overflow / flipped count) and
logged + `debug_assert!`ed at our call site. The allocation still proceeds — this only surfaces “getting suspiciously big” early in dev. 512 MB is far past any legitimate single buffer in this renderer. Only consulted under`debug_assertions`/ the`harden-diag`feature. See`MAX_GPU_BUFFER_BYTES`

# lru 0.18.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/lru/0.18.0

# LRU Cache

An implementation of a LRU cache. The cache supports `put`, `get`, `get_mut` and `pop` operations,
all of which are O(1). This crate was heavily influenced by the [LRU Cache implementation in an
earlier version of Rust's std::collections crate](https://doc.rust-lang.org/0.12.0/std/collections/lru_cache/struct.LruCache.html).

The MSRV for this crate is 1.85.0.

## Example

Below is a simple example of how to instantiate and use a LRU cache.

```
extern crate lru;
use LruCache;
use NonZeroUsize;
```

# lru - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/lru/0.18.0/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/lru/

## Expand description

An implementation of a LRU cache. The cache supports `get`, `get_mut`, `put`,
and `pop` operations, all of which are O(1). This crate was heavily influenced
by the [LRU Cache implementation in an earlier version of Rust’s std::collections crate](https://doc.rust-lang.org/0.12.0/std/collections/lru_cache/struct.LruCache.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
extern crate lru;
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
fn main() {
        let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
        cache.put("apple", 3);
        cache.put("banana", 2);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"apple").unwrap(), 3);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 2);
        assert!(cache.get(&"pear").is_none());
        assert_eq!(cache.put("banana", 4), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(cache.put("pear", 5), None);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"pear").unwrap(), 5);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 4);
        assert!(cache.get(&"apple").is_none());
        {
            let v = cache.get_mut(&"banana").unwrap();
            *v = 6;
        }
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 6);
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Into](https://docs.rs/struct.IntoIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator that moves out of a `LruCache`.
- [Iter](https://docs.rs/struct.Iter.html)
- An iterator over the entries of a `LruCache`.
- [IterMut](https://docs.rs/struct.IterMut.html)
- An iterator over mutables entries of a `LruCache`.
- [LruCache](https://docs.rs/struct.LruCache.html)
- An LRU Cache

[186](https://docs.rs#186)/// An LRU Cache
[187](https://docs.rs#187)pub struct LruCache<K, V, S = DefaultHasher> {
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    map: HashMap<KeyRef<K>, NonNull<LruEntry<K, V>>, S>,
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    cap: NonZeroUsize,
[190](https://docs.rs#190)
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    // head and tail are sigil nodes to facilitate inserting entries
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    head: *mut LruEntry<K, V>,
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    tail: *mut LruEntry<K, V>,
[194](https://docs.rs#194)}
[195](https://docs.rs#195)
[196](https://docs.rs#196)impl<K, V, S> Clone for LruCache<K, V, S>
[197](https://docs.rs#197)where
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    K: Hash + PartialEq + Eq + Clone,
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    V: Clone,
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    S: BuildHasher + Clone,
[201](https://docs.rs#201){
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
[203](https://docs.rs#203)        let map_cap = if self.is_unbounded() {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)            self.len()
[205](https://docs.rs#205)        } else {
[206](https://docs.rs#206)            self.cap().get()
[207](https://docs.rs#207)        };
[208](https://docs.rs#208)        let mut new_lru = LruCache::construct(
[209](https://docs.rs#209)            self.cap(),
[210](https://docs.rs#210)            HashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(map_cap, self.map.hasher().clone()),
[211](https://docs.rs#211)        );
[212](https://docs.rs#212)
[213](https://docs.rs#213)        for (key, value) in self.iter().rev() {
[214](https://docs.rs#214)            new_lru.push(key.clone(), value.clone());
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        }
[216](https://docs.rs#216)
[217](https://docs.rs#217)        new_lru
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    }
[219](https://docs.rs#219)}

[222](https://docs.rs#222)    /// Creates a new LRU Cache that holds at most `cap` items.
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    ///
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    /// # Example
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    ///

[230](https://docs.rs#230)    /// ```
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    pub fn new(cap: NonZeroUsize) -> LruCache<K, V> {
[232](https://docs.rs#232)        LruCache::construct(cap, HashMap::with_capacity(cap.get()))
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    }
[234](https://docs.rs#234)
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    /// Creates a new LRU Cache that never automatically evicts items.
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    ///
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    /// # Example
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    ///

[244](https://docs.rs#244)    pub fn unbounded() -> LruCache<K, V> {

[246](https://docs.rs#246)    }

[249](https://docs.rs#249)impl<K: Hash + Eq, V, S: BuildHasher> LruCache<K, V, S> {
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    /// Creates a new LRU Cache that holds at most `cap` items and
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    /// uses the provided hash builder to hash keys.
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    ///
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    /// # Example
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    ///
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    /// ```
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    /// use lru::{LruCache, DefaultHasher};
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    ///
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    /// let s = DefaultHasher::default();
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    /// let mut cache: LruCache<isize, &str> = LruCache::with_hasher(NonZeroUsize::new(10).unwrap(), s);
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    /// ```
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    pub fn with_hasher(cap: NonZeroUsize, hash_builder: S) -> LruCache<K, V, S> {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)        LruCache::construct(
[264](https://docs.rs#264)            cap,
[265](https://docs.rs#265)            HashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(cap.into(), hash_builder),
[266](https://docs.rs#266)        )
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    }
[268](https://docs.rs#268)
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// Creates a new LRU Cache that never automatically evicts items and
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    /// uses the provided hash builder to hash keys.
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    ///
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    /// # Example
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    ///
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    /// ```
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    /// use lru::{LruCache, DefaultHasher};
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    ///
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    /// let s = DefaultHasher::default();
[278](https://docs.rs#278)    /// let mut cache: LruCache<isize, &str> = LruCache::unbounded_with_hasher(s);
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    /// ```
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    pub fn unbounded_with_hasher(hash_builder: S) -> LruCache<K, V, S> {
[281](https://docs.rs#281)        LruCache::construct(NonZeroUsize::MAX, HashMap::with_hasher(hash_builder))
[282](https://docs.rs#282)    }
[283](https://docs.rs#283)
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    /// Creates a new LRU Cache with the given capacity.
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    fn construct(
[286](https://docs.rs#286)        cap: NonZeroUsize,
[287](https://docs.rs#287)        map: HashMap<KeyRef<K>, NonNull<LruEntry<K, V>>, S>,
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    ) -> LruCache<K, V, S> {
[289](https://docs.rs#289)        // NB: The compiler warns that cache does not need to be marked as mutable if we
[290](https://docs.rs#290)        // declare it as such since we only mutate it inside the unsafe block.
[291](https://docs.rs#291)        let cache = LruCache {
[292](https://docs.rs#292)            map,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            cap,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)            head: Box::into_raw(Box::new(LruEntry::new_sigil())),
[295](https://docs.rs#295)            tail: Box::into_raw(Box::new(LruEntry::new_sigil())),
[296](https://docs.rs#296)        };
[297](https://docs.rs#297)
[298](https://docs.rs#298)        unsafe {
[299](https://docs.rs#299)            (*cache.head).next = cache.tail;
[300](https://docs.rs#300)            (*cache.tail).prev = cache.head;
[301](https://docs.rs#301)        }
[302](https://docs.rs#302)
[303](https://docs.rs#303)        cache
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    }
[305](https://docs.rs#305)
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    /// Whether this LRU cache is unbounded.
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    fn is_unbounded(&self) -> bool {
[308](https://docs.rs#308)        self.cap() == NonZeroUsize::MAX
[309](https://docs.rs#309)    }
[310](https://docs.rs#310)
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    /// Puts a key-value pair into cache. If the key already exists in the cache, then it updates
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    /// the key's value and returns the old value. Otherwise, `None` is returned.
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    ///
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    /// # Example
[315](https://docs.rs#315)    ///
[316](https://docs.rs#316)    /// ```
[317](https://docs.rs#317)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[319](https://docs.rs#319)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[320](https://docs.rs#320)    ///
[321](https://docs.rs#321)    /// assert_eq!(None, cache.put(1, "a"));
[322](https://docs.rs#322)    /// assert_eq!(None, cache.put(2, "b"));
[323](https://docs.rs#323)    /// assert_eq!(Some("b"), cache.put(2, "beta"));
[324](https://docs.rs#324)    ///
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&1), Some(&"a"));
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&2), Some(&"beta"));
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    /// ```
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    pub fn put(&mut self, k: K, v: V) -> Option<V> {
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        self.capturing_put(k, v, false).map(|(_, v)| v)
[330](https://docs.rs#330)    }
[331](https://docs.rs#331)
[332](https://docs.rs#332)    /// Pushes a key-value pair into the cache. If an entry with key `k` already exists in
[333](https://docs.rs#333)    /// the cache or another cache entry is removed (due to the lru's capacity),
[334](https://docs.rs#334)    /// then it returns the old entry's key-value pair. Otherwise, returns `None`.
[335](https://docs.rs#335)    ///
[336](https://docs.rs#336)    /// # Example
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    ///
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    /// ```
[339](https://docs.rs#339)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[340](https://docs.rs#340)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[341](https://docs.rs#341)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[342](https://docs.rs#342)    ///
[343](https://docs.rs#343)    /// assert_eq!(None, cache.push(1, "a"));
[344](https://docs.rs#344)    /// assert_eq!(None, cache.push(2, "b"));
[345](https://docs.rs#345)    ///
[346](https://docs.rs#346)    /// // This push call returns (2, "b") because that was previously 2's entry in the cache.
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    /// assert_eq!(Some((2, "b")), cache.push(2, "beta"));
[348](https://docs.rs#348)    ///
[349](https://docs.rs#349)    /// // This push call returns (1, "a") because the cache is at capacity and 1's entry was the lru entry.
[350](https://docs.rs#350)    /// assert_eq!(Some((1, "a")), cache.push(3, "alpha"));
[351](https://docs.rs#351)    ///
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&1), None);
[353](https://docs.rs#353)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&2), Some(&"beta"));
[354](https://docs.rs#354)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&3), Some(&"alpha"));
[355](https://docs.rs#355)    /// ```
[356](https://docs.rs#356)    pub fn push(&mut self, k: K, v: V) -> Option<(K, V)> {
[357](https://docs.rs#357)        self.capturing_put(k, v, true)
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    }
[359](https://docs.rs#359)
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    // Used internally by `put` and `push` to add a new entry to the lru.
[361](https://docs.rs#361)    // Takes ownership of and returns entries replaced due to the cache's capacity
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    // when `capture` is true.
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    fn capturing_put(&mut self, k: K, mut v: V, capture: bool) -> Option<(K, V)> {
[364](https://docs.rs#364)        let node_ref = self.map.get_mut(&KeyRef { k: &k });
[365](https://docs.rs#365)
[366](https://docs.rs#366)        match node_ref {
[367](https://docs.rs#367)            Some(node_ref) => {
[368](https://docs.rs#368)                // if the key is already in the cache just update its value and move it to the
[369](https://docs.rs#369)                // front of the list
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node_ref.as_ptr();
[371](https://docs.rs#371)
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                // gets a reference to the node to perform a swap and drops it right after
[373](https://docs.rs#373)                let node_ref = unsafe { &mut (*(*node_ptr).val.as_mut_ptr()) };
[374](https://docs.rs#374)                mem::swap(&mut v, node_ref);
[375](https://docs.rs#375)                let _ = node_ref;
[376](https://docs.rs#376)
[377](https://docs.rs#377)                self.detach(node_ptr);
[378](https://docs.rs#378)                self.attach(node_ptr);
[379](https://docs.rs#379)                Some((k, v))
[380](https://docs.rs#380)            }
[381](https://docs.rs#381)            None => {
[382](https://docs.rs#382)                let (replaced, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k, v);
[383](https://docs.rs#383)                let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[384](https://docs.rs#384)
[385](https://docs.rs#385)                self.attach(node_ptr);
[386](https://docs.rs#386)
[387](https://docs.rs#387)                let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[388](https://docs.rs#388)                self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[389](https://docs.rs#389)
[390](https://docs.rs#390)                replaced.filter(|_| capture)
[391](https://docs.rs#391)            }
[392](https://docs.rs#392)        }
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    }
[394](https://docs.rs#394)
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    // Used internally to swap out a node if the cache is full or to create a new node if space
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    // is available. Shared between `put`, `push`, `get_or_insert`, and `get_or_insert_mut`.
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    fn replace_or_create_node(&mut self, k: K, v: V) -> (Option<(K, V)>, NonNull<LruEntry<K, V>>) {
[399](https://docs.rs#399)        if self.len() == self.cap().get() {
[400](https://docs.rs#400)            // if the cache is full, remove the last entry so we can use it for the new key
[401](https://docs.rs#401)            let old_key = KeyRef {
[402](https://docs.rs#402)                k: unsafe { &(*(*(*self.tail).prev).key.as_ptr()) },
[403](https://docs.rs#403)            };
[404](https://docs.rs#404)            let old_node = self.map.remove(&old_key).unwrap();
[405](https://docs.rs#405)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = old_node.as_ptr();
[406](https://docs.rs#406)
[407](https://docs.rs#407)            // read out the node's old key and value and then replace it
[408](https://docs.rs#408)            let replaced = unsafe {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)                (
[410](https://docs.rs#410)                    mem::replace(&mut (*node_ptr).key, mem::MaybeUninit::new(k)).assume_init(),
[411](https://docs.rs#411)                    mem::replace(&mut (*node_ptr).val, mem::MaybeUninit::new(v)).assume_init(),
[412](https://docs.rs#412)                )
[413](https://docs.rs#413)            };
[414](https://docs.rs#414)
[415](https://docs.rs#415)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[416](https://docs.rs#416)
[417](https://docs.rs#417)            (Some(replaced), old_node)
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        } else {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)            // if the cache is not full allocate a new LruEntry
[420](https://docs.rs#420)            // Safety: We allocate, turn into raw, and get NonNull all in one step.
[421](https://docs.rs#421)            (None, unsafe {
[422](https://docs.rs#422)                NonNull::new_unchecked(Box::into_raw(Box::new(LruEntry::new(k, v))))
[423](https://docs.rs#423)            })
[424](https://docs.rs#424)        }
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    }

[427](https://docs.rs#427)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache or `None` if it is not

[587](https://docs.rs#587)    /// use lru::LruCache;

[600](https://docs.rs#600)    /// ```
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    pub fn get_or_insert<F>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> &V
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    where
[603](https://docs.rs#603)        F: FnOnce() -> V,
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    {
[605](https://docs.rs#605)        self.get_or_insert_with_key(k, |_| f())
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    }
[607](https://docs.rs#607)
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used by passing
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    /// a reference to the key to populate the list and a reference is returned.
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    ///
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    /// # Example
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    ///
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    /// ```
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    ///
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    /// cache.put("One", 1);
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    /// cache.put("Two", 2);
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    /// cache.put("Two", 3);
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    /// cache.put("Three", 4);
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    ///
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("Two", |_|1), &3);
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("Three", |k|k.len()), &4);
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("One", |_|1), &1);
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("One", |k|k.len()), &1);
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    /// ```
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    pub fn get_or_insert_with_key<F>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> &V
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    where
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        F: FnOnce(&K) -> V,
[633](https://docs.rs#633)    {
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(&KeyRef { k: &k }) {
[635](https://docs.rs#635)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[636](https://docs.rs#636)
[637](https://docs.rs#637)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[638](https://docs.rs#638)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[639](https://docs.rs#639)
[640](https://docs.rs#640)            unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() }
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        } else {
[642](https://docs.rs#642)            let v = f(&k);
[643](https://docs.rs#643)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k, v);
[644](https://docs.rs#644)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[645](https://docs.rs#645)
[646](https://docs.rs#646)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[647](https://docs.rs#647)
[648](https://docs.rs#648)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[649](https://docs.rs#649)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[650](https://docs.rs#650)            unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() }
[651](https://docs.rs#651)        }
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    }
[653](https://docs.rs#653)
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used to populate
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    /// the list and a reference is returned. The value referenced by the
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    /// key is only cloned (using `to_owned()`) if it doesn't exist in the
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    /// cache.
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    ///
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    /// # Example
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    ///
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    /// ```
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    /// use std::rc::Rc;
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    ///
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    /// let key1 = Rc::new("1".to_owned());
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    /// let key2 = Rc::new("2".to_owned());
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::<Rc<String>, String>::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key1, ||"One".to_owned()), "One");
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key2, ||"Two".to_owned()), "Two");
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key2, ||"Not two".to_owned()), "Two");
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key2, ||"Again not two".to_owned()), "Two");
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    /// assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key1), 2);
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    /// assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key2), 2); // key2 was only cloned once even though we
[677](https://docs.rs#677)    ///                                         // queried it 3 times
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    /// ```
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    pub fn get_or_insert_ref<'a, Q, F>(&'a mut self, k: &'_ Q, f: F) -> &'a V
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    where
[681](https://docs.rs#681)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[682](https://docs.rs#682)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized + alloc::borrow::ToOwned<Owned = K>,
[683](https://docs.rs#683)        F: FnOnce() -> V,
[684](https://docs.rs#684)    {
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[686](https://docs.rs#686)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[687](https://docs.rs#687)
[688](https://docs.rs#688)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[689](https://docs.rs#689)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[690](https://docs.rs#690)
[691](https://docs.rs#691)            unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() }
[692](https://docs.rs#692)        } else {
[693](https://docs.rs#693)            let v = f();
[694](https://docs.rs#694)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k.to_owned(), v);
[695](https://docs.rs#695)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[696](https://docs.rs#696)
[697](https://docs.rs#697)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[698](https://docs.rs#698)
[699](https://docs.rs#699)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[700](https://docs.rs#700)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[701](https://docs.rs#701)            unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() }
[702](https://docs.rs#702)        }
[703](https://docs.rs#703)    }
[704](https://docs.rs#704)
[705](https://docs.rs#705)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[706](https://docs.rs#706)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[707](https://docs.rs#707)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used to populate
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    /// the list and a reference is returned. If `FnOnce` returns `Err`,
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    /// returns the `Err`.
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    ///
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    /// # Example
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    ///
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    /// ```
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    /// use lru::LruCache;

[717](https://docs.rs#717)    ///
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    /// cache.put(1, "a");
[719](https://docs.rs#719)    /// cache.put(2, "b");
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    /// cache.put(2, "c");
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    /// cache.put(3, "d");
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    ///
[723](https://docs.rs#723)    /// let f = ||->Result<&str, String> {Err("failed".to_owned())};

[725](https://docs.rs#725)    /// let b = ||->Result<&str, String> {Ok("b")};
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert(2, a), Ok(&"c"));
[727](https://docs.rs#727)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert(3, a), Ok(&"d"));
[728](https://docs.rs#728)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert(4, f), Err("failed".to_owned()));
[729](https://docs.rs#729)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert(5, b), Ok(&"b"));
[730](https://docs.rs#730)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert(5, a), Ok(&"b"));
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    /// ```
[732](https://docs.rs#732)    pub fn try_get_or_insert<F, E>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> Result<&V, E>
[733](https://docs.rs#733)    where
[734](https://docs.rs#734)        F: FnOnce() -> Result<V, E>,
[735](https://docs.rs#735)    {
[736](https://docs.rs#736)        self.try_get_or_insert_with_key(k, |_| f())

[739](https://docs.rs#739)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[740](https://docs.rs#740)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used by passing
[742](https://docs.rs#742)    /// a reference to the key to populate the list and a reference is returned.
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    /// If `FnOnce` returns `Err`, returns the `Err`.
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    ///
[745](https://docs.rs#745)    /// # Example
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    ///
[747](https://docs.rs#747)    /// ```
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[749](https://docs.rs#749)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[750](https://docs.rs#750)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[751](https://docs.rs#751)    ///
[752](https://docs.rs#752)    /// cache.put("One", 1);
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    /// cache.put("Two", 2);
[754](https://docs.rs#754)    /// cache.put("Two", 3);
[755](https://docs.rs#755)    /// cache.put("Three", 4);
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    ///
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    /// let f = |_: &&str|->Result<usize, String> {Err("failed".to_owned())};
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    /// let len = |k: &&str|->Result<usize, String> {Ok(k.len())};
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    /// let zero = |_: &&str|->Result<usize, String> {Ok(0)};
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_with_key("Two", len), Ok(&3));
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_with_key("Three", len), Ok(&4));
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_with_key("Four", f), Err("failed".to_owned()));
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_with_key("Five", len), Ok(&4));
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_with_key("Five", zero), Ok(&4));
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    /// ```
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    pub fn try_get_or_insert_with_key<F, E>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> Result<&V, E>
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    where
[768](https://docs.rs#768)        F: FnOnce(&K) -> Result<V, E>,
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    {
[770](https://docs.rs#770)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(&KeyRef { k: &k }) {
[771](https://docs.rs#771)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[772](https://docs.rs#772)
[773](https://docs.rs#773)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[774](https://docs.rs#774)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[775](https://docs.rs#775)
[776](https://docs.rs#776)            unsafe { Ok(&*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr()) }
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        } else {
[778](https://docs.rs#778)            let v = f(&k)?;
[779](https://docs.rs#779)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k, v);
[780](https://docs.rs#780)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[781](https://docs.rs#781)
[782](https://docs.rs#782)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[783](https://docs.rs#783)
[784](https://docs.rs#784)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[785](https://docs.rs#785)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[786](https://docs.rs#786)            Ok(unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() })
[787](https://docs.rs#787)        }
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    }
[789](https://docs.rs#789)
[790](https://docs.rs#790)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[792](https://docs.rs#792)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used to populate
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    /// the list and a reference is returned. If `FnOnce` returns `Err`,
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    /// returns the `Err`. The value referenced by the key is only cloned
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    /// (using `to_owned()`) if it doesn't exist in the cache and `FnOnce`
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    /// succeeds.
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    ///
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    /// # Example
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    ///
[800](https://docs.rs#800)    /// ```
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[802](https://docs.rs#802)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    /// use std::rc::Rc;
[804](https://docs.rs#804)    ///
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    /// let key1 = Rc::new("1".to_owned());
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    /// let key2 = Rc::new("2".to_owned());
[807](https://docs.rs#807)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::<Rc<String>, String>::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[808](https://docs.rs#808)    /// let f = ||->Result<String, ()> {Err(())};
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    /// let a = ||->Result<String, ()> {Ok("One".to_owned())};
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    /// let b = ||->Result<String, ()> {Ok("Two".to_owned())};
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_ref(&key1, a), Ok(&"One".to_owned()));
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_ref(&key2, f), Err(()));
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_ref(&key2, b), Ok(&"Two".to_owned()));
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_ref(&key2, a), Ok(&"Two".to_owned()));
[815](https://docs.rs#815)    /// assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key1), 2);
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    /// assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key2), 2); // key2 was only cloned once even though we
[817](https://docs.rs#817)    ///                                         // queried it 3 times
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    /// ```
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    pub fn try_get_or_insert_ref<'a, Q, F, E>(&'a mut self, k: &'_ Q, f: F) -> Result<&'a V, E>
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    where
[821](https://docs.rs#821)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[822](https://docs.rs#822)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized + alloc::borrow::ToOwned<Owned = K>,
[823](https://docs.rs#823)        F: FnOnce() -> Result<V, E>,
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    {
[825](https://docs.rs#825)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[826](https://docs.rs#826)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[827](https://docs.rs#827)
[828](https://docs.rs#828)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[829](https://docs.rs#829)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[830](https://docs.rs#830)
[831](https://docs.rs#831)            unsafe { Ok(&*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr()) }
[832](https://docs.rs#832)        } else {
[833](https://docs.rs#833)            let v = f()?;
[834](https://docs.rs#834)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k.to_owned(), v);
[835](https://docs.rs#835)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[836](https://docs.rs#836)
[837](https://docs.rs#837)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[838](https://docs.rs#838)
[839](https://docs.rs#839)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[840](https://docs.rs#840)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[841](https://docs.rs#841)            Ok(unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() })
[842](https://docs.rs#842)        }
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    }

[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)        } else {
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)            let v = f(&k)?;
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k, v);
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)            unsafe { Ok(&mut *(*node_ptr).val.as_mut_ptr()) }
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)        }
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)    }
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)    /// Returns a mutable reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used to populate
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)    /// the list and a mutable reference is returned. If `FnOnce` returns `Err`,
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)    /// returns the `Err`. The value referenced by the key is only cloned
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)    /// (using `to_owned()`) if it doesn't exist in the cache and `FnOnce`
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)    /// succeeds.
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)    ///
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)    /// # Example
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)    ///
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)    /// ```
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)    /// use std::rc::Rc;
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)    ///
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)    /// let key1 = Rc::new("1".to_owned());
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)    /// let key2 = Rc::new("2".to_owned());
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::<Rc<String>, String>::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)    /// let f = ||->Result<String, ()> {Err(())};
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)    /// let a = ||->Result<String, ()> {Ok("One".to_owned())};
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)    /// let b = ||->Result<String, ()> {Ok("Two".to_owned())};
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_mut_ref(&key1, a), Ok(&mut "One".to_owned()));
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_mut_ref(&key2, f), Err(()));
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)    /// if let Ok(v) = cache.try_get_or_insert_mut_ref(&key2, b) {
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)    ///     *v = "New two".to_owned();
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)    /// }
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_mut_ref(&key2, a), Ok(&mut "New two".to_owned()));
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)    /// assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key1), 2);
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)    /// assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key2), 2); // key2 was only cloned once even though we
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)    ///                                         // queried it 3 times
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)    /// ```
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)    pub fn try_get_or_insert_mut_ref<'a, Q, F, E>(
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)        &'a mut self,
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)        k: &'_ Q,
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)        f: F,
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)    ) -> Result<&'a mut V, E>
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)    where
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized + alloc::borrow::ToOwned<Owned = K>,
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)        F: FnOnce() -> Result<V, E>,
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)    {
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)            unsafe { Ok(&mut *(*node_ptr).val.as_mut_ptr()) }
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)        } else {
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)            let v = f()?;
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k.to_owned(), v);
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)            unsafe { Ok(&mut *(*node_ptr).val.as_mut_ptr()) }
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)        }
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)    }
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)    /// Returns a reference to the value corresponding to the key in the cache or `None` if it is
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)    /// not present in the cache. Unlike `get`, `peek` does not update the LRU list so the key's
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)    /// position will be unchanged.
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)    ///
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)    /// # Example
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)    ///
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)    /// ```
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)    ///
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)    /// cache.put(1, "a");
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)    /// cache.put(2, "b");
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)    ///
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)    /// assert_eq!(cache.peek(&1), Some(&"a"));
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)    /// assert_eq!(cache.peek(&2), Some(&"b"));
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)    /// ```
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)    pub fn peek<'a, Q>(&'a self, k: &Q) -> Option<&'a V>
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)    where
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)    {
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)        self.map
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)            .get(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k))
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)            .map(|node| unsafe { &*node.as_ref().val.as_ptr() })
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)    }

[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)    /// Returns a mutable reference to the value corresponding to the key in the cache or `None`

[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)        if self.is_empty() {
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)            return None;
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)        }
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)        let (key, val);
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)        unsafe {
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)            let node = (*self.tail).prev;
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)            key = &(*(*node).key.as_ptr()) as &K;
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)            val = &(*(*node).val.as_ptr()) as &V;
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)        }

[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)        Some((key, val))
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)    }

[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)    /// Removes and returns the value corresponding to the key from the cache or

[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)    pub fn pop<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> Option<V>
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)    where
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)    {
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)        match self.map.remove(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)            None => None,
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)            Some(old_node) => {
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)                let mut old_node = unsafe {
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)                    let mut old_node = *Box::from_raw(old_node.as_ptr());
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)                    ptr::drop_in_place(old_node.key.as_mut_ptr());

[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)                let LruEntry { key: _, val, .. } = old_node;
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)                unsafe { Some(val.assume_init()) }
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)            }
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)        }
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)    }

[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)    pub fn pop_entry<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> Option<(K, V)>

[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)    ///

[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)    /// cache.put(4, "c");
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)    /// cache.get(&3);
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)    ///

[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)    /// assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), None);
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)    /// assert_eq!(cache.len(), 0);
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)    /// ```
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)    pub fn pop_lru(&mut self) -> Option<(K, V)> {
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)        let node = self.remove_last()?;
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)        // N.B.: Can't destructure directly because of https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/28536
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)        let node = *node;
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)        let LruEntry { key, val, .. } = node;
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)        unsafe { Some((key.assume_init(), val.assume_init())) }
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)    }
