Attempts to get mutable references to `N` values in the map at once.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/hashbrown/table.rs.html#1548-1554)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/hashbrown/table.rs.html#1548-1554)

Attempts to get mutable references to `N` values in the map at once, without validating that
the values are unique.

The `eq` argument should be a closure such that `eq(i, k)` returns true if `k` is equal to
the `i`th key to be looked up.

Returns an array of length `N` with the results of each query. `None` will be returned if
any of the keys are missing.

For a safe alternative see [ get_disjoint_mut](https://docs.rs/struct.HashTable.html#method.get_disjoint_mut).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-3)Safety

Calling this method with overlapping keys is * undefined behavior* even if the resulting
references are not used.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```
use hashbrown::hash_table::Entry;
use hashbrown::{HashTable, DefaultHashBuilder};
use std::hash::BuildHasher;
let mut libraries: HashTable<(&str, u32)> = HashTable::new();
let hasher = DefaultHashBuilder::default();
let hasher = |val: &_| hasher.hash_one(val);
for (k, v) in [
    ("Bodleian Library", 1602),
    ("Athenæum", 1807),
    ("Herzogin-Anna-Amalia-Bibliothek", 1691),
    ("Library of Congress", 1800),
] {
    libraries.insert_unique(hasher(&k), (k, v), |(k, _)| hasher(&k));
}
let keys = ["Athenæum", "Library of Congress"];
let got = libraries.get_disjoint_mut(keys.map(|k| hasher(&k)), |i, val| keys[i] == val.0);
assert_eq!(
    got,
    [Some(&mut ("Athenæum", 1807)), Some(&mut ("Library of Congress", 1800))],
);
// Missing keys result in None
let keys = ["Athenæum", "New York Public Library"];
let got = libraries.get_disjoint_mut(keys.map(|k| hasher(&k)), |i, val| keys[i] == val.0);
assert_eq!(got, [Some(&mut ("Athenæum", 1807)), None]);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/hashbrown/table.rs.html#1559-1565)use `get_disjoint_unchecked_mut` instead

use `get_disjoint_unchecked_mut` instead

# lazy_static - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lazy_static/^1.0/

## Expand description

A macro for declaring lazily evaluated statics.

Using this macro, it is possible to have `static`s that require code to be
executed at runtime in order to be initialized.
This includes anything requiring heap allocations, like vectors or hash maps,
as well as anything that requires function calls to be computed.

[§](https://docs.rs#syntax)Syntax

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
lazy_static! {
    [pub] static ref NAME_1: TYPE_1 = EXPR_1;
    [pub] static ref NAME_2: TYPE_2 = EXPR_2;
    ...
    [pub] static ref NAME_N: TYPE_N = EXPR_N;
}
```
Attributes (including doc comments) are supported as well:

```
use lazy_static::lazy_static;
lazy_static! {
    /// This is an example for using doc comment attributes
    static ref EXAMPLE: u8 = 42;
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#semantics)Semantics

For a given `static ref NAME: TYPE = EXPR;`, the macro generates a unique type that
implements `Deref<TYPE>` and stores it in a static with name `NAME`. (Attributes end up
attaching to this type.)

On first deref, `EXPR` gets evaluated and stored internally, such that all further derefs
can return a reference to the same object. Note that this can lead to deadlocks
if you have multiple lazy statics that depend on each other in their initialization.

Apart from the lazy initialization, the resulting “static ref” variables have generally the same properties as regular “static” variables:

- Any type in them needs to fulfill the `Sync`trait.
- If the type has a destructor, then it will not run when the process exits.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Using the macro:

```
use lazy_static::lazy_static;
use std::collections::HashMap;
lazy_static! {
    static ref HASHMAP: HashMap<u32, &'static str> = {
        let mut m = HashMap::new();
        m.insert(0, "foo");
        m.insert(1, "bar");
        m.insert(2, "baz");
        m
    };
    static ref COUNT: usize = HASHMAP.len();
    static ref NUMBER: u32 = times_two(21);
}
fn times_two(n: u32) -> u32 { n * 2 }
fn main() {
    println!("The map has {} entries.", *COUNT);
    println!("The entry for `0` is \"{}\".", HASHMAP.get(&0).unwrap());
    println!("A expensive calculation on a static results in: {}.", *NUMBER);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#implementation-details)Implementation details

The `Deref` implementation uses a hidden static variable that is guarded by an atomic check on each access.

[§](https://docs.rs#cargo-features)Cargo features

This crate provides one cargo feature:

- `spin_no_std`: This allows using this crate in a no-std environment, by depending on the standalone- `spin`crate.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Lazy](https://docs.rs/trait.LazyStatic.html)- Static
- Support trait for enabling a few common operation on lazy static values.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [initialize](https://docs.rs/fn.initialize.html)
- Takes a shared reference to a lazy static and initializes it if it has not been already.

# scoped_threadpool - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/scoped_threadpool/0.1.9/target-redirect/scoped_threadpool/

## Expand description

This crate provides a stable, safe and scoped threadpool.

It can be used to execute a number of short-lived jobs in parallel without the need to respawn the underlying threads.

Jobs are runnable by borrowing the pool for a given scope, during which
an arbitrary number of them can be executed. These jobs can access data of
any lifetime outside of the pools scope, which allows working on
non-`'static` references in parallel.

For safety reasons, a panic inside a worker thread will not be isolated, but rather propagate to the outside of the pool.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples:

```
extern crate scoped_threadpool;
use scoped_threadpool::Pool;
fn main() {
    // Create a threadpool holding 4 threads
    let mut pool = Pool::new(4);
    let mut vec = vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
    // Use the threads as scoped threads that can
    // reference anything outside this closure
    pool.scoped(|scope| {
        // Create references to each element in the vector ...
        for e in &mut vec {
            // ... and add 1 to it in a seperate thread
            scope.execute(move || {
                *e += 1;
            });
        }
    });
    assert_eq!(vec, vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]);
}
```

# stats_alloc 0.1.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/stats_alloc/0.1.10

# stats_alloc

An instrumenting middleware for global allocators in Rust, useful in testing for validating assumptions regarding allocation patterns, and potentially in production loads to monitor for memory leaks.

## Example

```
extern crate stats_alloc;
use ;
use System;
static GLOBAL: & = &INSTRUMENTED_SYSTEM;
```
## Custom allocators

Currenty wrapping a custom allocator requires the use of the nightly compiler
and compiling with the "nightly" feature due to the soon to stabilize use of
the unstable `const_fn_trait_bound` and the fact that the internals of the
instrumenting type are not public. If that's fine with you, a custom allocator
can be wrapped as follows:

```
static GLOBAL:  = new;
```

# stats_alloc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/stats_alloc/0.1.10/target-redirect/stats_alloc/

## Expand description

An instrumenting middleware for global allocators in Rust, useful in testing for validating assumptions regarding allocation patterns, and potentially in production loads to monitor for memory leaks.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
extern crate stats_alloc;
use stats_alloc::{Region, StatsAlloc, INSTRUMENTED_SYSTEM};
use std::alloc::System;
#[global_allocator]
static GLOBAL: &StatsAlloc<System> = &INSTRUMENTED_SYSTEM;
fn main() {
    let reg = Region::new(&GLOBAL);
    let x: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(1_024);
    println!("Stats at 1: {:#?}", reg.change());
    // Used here to ensure that the value is not
    // dropped before we check the statistics
    ::std::mem::size_of_val(&x);
}
```

Allocator statistics

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.allocations)

`allocations: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)Count of allocation operations

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.deallocations)

`deallocations: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)Count of deallocation operations

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.reallocations)

`reallocations: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)Count of reallocation operations

An example where reallocation may occur: resizing of a `Vec<T>` when
its length would excceed its capacity. Excessive reallocations may
indicate that resizable data structures are being created with
insufficient or poorly estimated initial capcities.

```
let mut x = Vec::with_capacity(1);
x.push(0);
x.push(1); // Potential reallocation
```
[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.bytes_allocated)

`bytes_allocated: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)Total bytes requested by allocations

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.bytes_deallocated)

`bytes_deallocated: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)Total bytes freed by deallocations

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.bytes_reallocated)

`bytes_reallocated: `[isize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.isize.html)Total of bytes requested minus bytes freed by reallocations

This number is positive if the total bytes requested by reallocation operations is greater than the total bytes freed by reallocations. A positive value indicates that resizable structures are growing, while a negative value indicates that such structures are shrinking.

# lru - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lru/0.18.0/aarch64-apple-darwin/lru/

## Expand description

An implementation of a LRU cache. The cache supports `get`, `get_mut`, `put`,
and `pop` operations, all of which are O(1). This crate was heavily influenced
by the [LRU Cache implementation in an earlier version of Rust’s std::collections crate](https://doc.rust-lang.org/0.12.0/std/collections/lru_cache/struct.LruCache.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
extern crate lru;
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
fn main() {
        let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
        cache.put("apple", 3);
        cache.put("banana", 2);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"apple").unwrap(), 3);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 2);
        assert!(cache.get(&"pear").is_none());
        assert_eq!(cache.put("banana", 4), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(cache.put("pear", 5), None);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"pear").unwrap(), 5);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 4);
        assert!(cache.get(&"apple").is_none());
        {
            let v = cache.get_mut(&"banana").unwrap();
            *v = 6;
        }
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 6);
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Into](https://docs.rs/struct.IntoIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator that moves out of a `LruCache`.
- [Iter](https://docs.rs/struct.Iter.html)
- An iterator over the entries of a `LruCache`.
- [IterMut](https://docs.rs/struct.IterMut.html)
- An iterator over mutables entries of a `LruCache`.
- [LruCache](https://docs.rs/struct.LruCache.html)
- An LRU Cache

[186](https://docs.rs#186)/// An LRU Cache
[187](https://docs.rs#187)pub struct LruCache<K, V, S = DefaultHasher> {
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    map: HashMap<KeyRef<K>, NonNull<LruEntry<K, V>>, S>,
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    cap: NonZeroUsize,
[190](https://docs.rs#190)
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    // head and tail are sigil nodes to facilitate inserting entries
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    head: *mut LruEntry<K, V>,

[194](https://docs.rs#194)}

[196](https://docs.rs#196)impl<K, V, S> Clone for LruCache<K, V, S>
[197](https://docs.rs#197)where
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    K: Hash + PartialEq + Eq + Clone,
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    V: Clone,
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    S: BuildHasher + Clone,
[201](https://docs.rs#201){
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
[203](https://docs.rs#203)        let map_cap = if self.is_unbounded() {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)            self.len()
[205](https://docs.rs#205)        } else {
[206](https://docs.rs#206)            self.cap().get()
[207](https://docs.rs#207)        };
[208](https://docs.rs#208)        let mut new_lru = LruCache::construct(
[209](https://docs.rs#209)            self.cap(),
[210](https://docs.rs#210)            HashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(map_cap, self.map.hasher().clone()),
[211](https://docs.rs#211)        );
[212](https://docs.rs#212)
[213](https://docs.rs#213)        for (key, value) in self.iter().rev() {
[214](https://docs.rs#214)            new_lru.push(key.clone(), value.clone());
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        }
[216](https://docs.rs#216)
[217](https://docs.rs#217)        new_lru
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    }

[250](https://docs.rs#250)    /// Creates a new LRU Cache that holds at most `cap` items and

[252](https://docs.rs#252)    ///

[254](https://docs.rs#254)    ///

[261](https://docs.rs#261)    /// ```
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    pub fn with_hasher(cap: NonZeroUsize, hash_builder: S) -> LruCache<K, V, S> {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)        LruCache::construct(
[264](https://docs.rs#264)            cap,
[265](https://docs.rs#265)            HashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(cap.into(), hash_builder),
[266](https://docs.rs#266)        )
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    }
[268](https://docs.rs#268)
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// Creates a new LRU Cache that never automatically evicts items and
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    /// uses the provided hash builder to hash keys.
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    ///
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    /// # Example
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    ///
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    /// ```
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    /// use lru::{LruCache, DefaultHasher};
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    ///
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    /// let s = DefaultHasher::default();

[279](https://docs.rs#279)    /// ```
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    pub fn unbounded_with_hasher(hash_builder: S) -> LruCache<K, V, S> {
[281](https://docs.rs#281)        LruCache::construct(NonZeroUsize::MAX, HashMap::with_hasher(hash_builder))
[282](https://docs.rs#282)    }
[283](https://docs.rs#283)
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    /// Creates a new LRU Cache with the given capacity.
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    fn construct(
[286](https://docs.rs#286)        cap: NonZeroUsize,
[287](https://docs.rs#287)        map: HashMap<KeyRef<K>, NonNull<LruEntry<K, V>>, S>,
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    ) -> LruCache<K, V, S> {
[289](https://docs.rs#289)        // NB: The compiler warns that cache does not need to be marked as mutable if we
[290](https://docs.rs#290)        // declare it as such since we only mutate it inside the unsafe block.
[291](https://docs.rs#291)        let cache = LruCache {
[292](https://docs.rs#292)            map,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            cap,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)            head: Box::into_raw(Box::new(LruEntry::new_sigil())),
[295](https://docs.rs#295)            tail: Box::into_raw(Box::new(LruEntry::new_sigil())),
[296](https://docs.rs#296)        };
[297](https://docs.rs#297)
[298](https://docs.rs#298)        unsafe {
[299](https://docs.rs#299)            (*cache.head).next = cache.tail;
[300](https://docs.rs#300)            (*cache.tail).prev = cache.head;
[301](https://docs.rs#301)        }
[302](https://docs.rs#302)
[303](https://docs.rs#303)        cache
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    }
[305](https://docs.rs#305)
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    /// Whether this LRU cache is unbounded.
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    fn is_unbounded(&self) -> bool {
[308](https://docs.rs#308)        self.cap() == NonZeroUsize::MAX
[309](https://docs.rs#309)    }
[310](https://docs.rs#310)
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    /// Puts a key-value pair into cache. If the key already exists in the cache, then it updates
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    /// the key's value and returns the old value. Otherwise, `None` is returned.
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    ///
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    /// # Example
[315](https://docs.rs#315)    ///
[316](https://docs.rs#316)    /// ```
[317](https://docs.rs#317)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[319](https://docs.rs#319)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[320](https://docs.rs#320)    ///
[321](https://docs.rs#321)    /// assert_eq!(None, cache.put(1, "a"));
[322](https://docs.rs#322)    /// assert_eq!(None, cache.put(2, "b"));
[323](https://docs.rs#323)    /// assert_eq!(Some("b"), cache.put(2, "beta"));
[324](https://docs.rs#324)    ///
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&1), Some(&"a"));
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&2), Some(&"beta"));
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    /// ```
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    pub fn put(&mut self, k: K, v: V) -> Option<V> {
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        self.capturing_put(k, v, false).map(|(_, v)| v)
[330](https://docs.rs#330)    }
[331](https://docs.rs#331)
[332](https://docs.rs#332)    /// Pushes a key-value pair into the cache. If an entry with key `k` already exists in
[333](https://docs.rs#333)    /// the cache or another cache entry is removed (due to the lru's capacity),
[334](https://docs.rs#334)    /// then it returns the old entry's key-value pair. Otherwise, returns `None`.
[335](https://docs.rs#335)    ///
[336](https://docs.rs#336)    /// # Example
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    ///
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    /// ```
[339](https://docs.rs#339)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[340](https://docs.rs#340)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[341](https://docs.rs#341)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[342](https://docs.rs#342)    ///
[343](https://docs.rs#343)    /// assert_eq!(None, cache.push(1, "a"));
[344](https://docs.rs#344)    /// assert_eq!(None, cache.push(2, "b"));
[345](https://docs.rs#345)    ///
[346](https://docs.rs#346)    /// // This push call returns (2, "b") because that was previously 2's entry in the cache.
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    /// assert_eq!(Some((2, "b")), cache.push(2, "beta"));
[348](https://docs.rs#348)    ///
[349](https://docs.rs#349)    /// // This push call returns (1, "a") because the cache is at capacity and 1's entry was the lru entry.
[350](https://docs.rs#350)    /// assert_eq!(Some((1, "a")), cache.push(3, "alpha"));
[351](https://docs.rs#351)    ///
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&1), None);
[353](https://docs.rs#353)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&2), Some(&"beta"));
[354](https://docs.rs#354)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&3), Some(&"alpha"));
[355](https://docs.rs#355)    /// ```
[356](https://docs.rs#356)    pub fn push(&mut self, k: K, v: V) -> Option<(K, V)> {
[357](https://docs.rs#357)        self.capturing_put(k, v, true)
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    }
[359](https://docs.rs#359)
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    // Used internally by `put` and `push` to add a new entry to the lru.
[361](https://docs.rs#361)    // Takes ownership of and returns entries replaced due to the cache's capacity
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    // when `capture` is true.
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    fn capturing_put(&mut self, k: K, mut v: V, capture: bool) -> Option<(K, V)> {
[364](https://docs.rs#364)        let node_ref = self.map.get_mut(&KeyRef { k: &k });
[365](https://docs.rs#365)
[366](https://docs.rs#366)        match node_ref {
[367](https://docs.rs#367)            Some(node_ref) => {
[368](https://docs.rs#368)                // if the key is already in the cache just update its value and move it to the
[369](https://docs.rs#369)                // front of the list
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node_ref.as_ptr();
[371](https://docs.rs#371)
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                // gets a reference to the node to perform a swap and drops it right after
[373](https://docs.rs#373)                let node_ref = unsafe { &mut (*(*node_ptr).val.as_mut_ptr()) };
[374](https://docs.rs#374)                mem::swap(&mut v, node_ref);
[375](https://docs.rs#375)                let _ = node_ref;
[376](https://docs.rs#376)
[377](https://docs.rs#377)                self.detach(node_ptr);
[378](https://docs.rs#378)                self.attach(node_ptr);
[379](https://docs.rs#379)                Some((k, v))
[380](https://docs.rs#380)            }
[381](https://docs.rs#381)            None => {
[382](https://docs.rs#382)                let (replaced, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k, v);
[383](https://docs.rs#383)                let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[384](https://docs.rs#384)
[385](https://docs.rs#385)                self.attach(node_ptr);
[386](https://docs.rs#386)
[387](https://docs.rs#387)                let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[388](https://docs.rs#388)                self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[389](https://docs.rs#389)
[390](https://docs.rs#390)                replaced.filter(|_| capture)
[391](https://docs.rs#391)            }
[392](https://docs.rs#392)        }
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    }
[394](https://docs.rs#394)
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    // Used internally to swap out a node if the cache is full or to create a new node if space
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    // is available. Shared between `put`, `push`, `get_or_insert`, and `get_or_insert_mut`.
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    fn replace_or_create_node(&mut self, k: K, v: V) -> (Option<(K, V)>, NonNull<LruEntry<K, V>>) {
[399](https://docs.rs#399)        if self.len() == self.cap().get() {
[400](https://docs.rs#400)            // if the cache is full, remove the last entry so we can use it for the new key
[401](https://docs.rs#401)            let old_key = KeyRef {
[402](https://docs.rs#402)                k: unsafe { &(*(*(*self.tail).prev).key.as_ptr()) },
[403](https://docs.rs#403)            };
[404](https://docs.rs#404)            let old_node = self.map.remove(&old_key).unwrap();
[405](https://docs.rs#405)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = old_node.as_ptr();
[406](https://docs.rs#406)
[407](https://docs.rs#407)            // read out the node's old key and value and then replace it
[408](https://docs.rs#408)            let replaced = unsafe {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)                (
[410](https://docs.rs#410)                    mem::replace(&mut (*node_ptr).key, mem::MaybeUninit::new(k)).assume_init(),
[411](https://docs.rs#411)                    mem::replace(&mut (*node_ptr).val, mem::MaybeUninit::new(v)).assume_init(),
[412](https://docs.rs#412)                )
[413](https://docs.rs#413)            };
[414](https://docs.rs#414)
[415](https://docs.rs#415)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[416](https://docs.rs#416)
[417](https://docs.rs#417)            (Some(replaced), old_node)
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        } else {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)            // if the cache is not full allocate a new LruEntry
[420](https://docs.rs#420)            // Safety: We allocate, turn into raw, and get NonNull all in one step.
[421](https://docs.rs#421)            (None, unsafe {
[422](https://docs.rs#422)                NonNull::new_unchecked(Box::into_raw(Box::new(LruEntry::new(k, v))))
[423](https://docs.rs#423)            })
[424](https://docs.rs#424)        }
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    }
[426](https://docs.rs#426)
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache or `None` if it is not
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    /// present in the cache. Moves the key to the head of the LRU list if it exists.
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    ///
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    /// # Example
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    ///
[432](https://docs.rs#432)    /// ```
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[435](https://docs.rs#435)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[436](https://docs.rs#436)    ///
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    /// cache.put(1, "a");
[438](https://docs.rs#438)    /// cache.put(2, "b");
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    /// cache.put(2, "c");
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    /// cache.put(3, "d");
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    ///
[442](https://docs.rs#442)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&1), None);
[443](https://docs.rs#443)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&2), Some(&"c"));
[444](https://docs.rs#444)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&3), Some(&"d"));
[445](https://docs.rs#445)    /// ```
[446](https://docs.rs#446)    pub fn get<'a, Q>(&'a mut self, k: &Q) -> Option<&'a V>
[447](https://docs.rs#447)    where
[448](https://docs.rs#448)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[449](https://docs.rs#449)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[450](https://docs.rs#450)    {
[451](https://docs.rs#451)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[452](https://docs.rs#452)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[453](https://docs.rs#453)
[454](https://docs.rs#454)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[455](https://docs.rs#455)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[456](https://docs.rs#456)
[457](https://docs.rs#457)            Some(unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() })
[458](https://docs.rs#458)        } else {
[459](https://docs.rs#459)            None
[460](https://docs.rs#460)        }
[461](https://docs.rs#461)    }
[462](https://docs.rs#462)
[463](https://docs.rs#463)    /// Returns a mutable reference to the value of the key in the cache or `None` if it
[464](https://docs.rs#464)    /// is not present in the cache. Moves the key to the head of the LRU list if it exists.
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    ///
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    /// # Example
[467](https://docs.rs#467)    ///
[468](https://docs.rs#468)    /// ```
[469](https://docs.rs#469)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[470](https://docs.rs#470)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[471](https://docs.rs#471)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[472](https://docs.rs#472)    ///
[473](https://docs.rs#473)    /// cache.put("apple", 8);
[474](https://docs.rs#474)    /// cache.put("banana", 4);
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    /// cache.put("banana", 6);
[476](https://docs.rs#476)    /// cache.put("pear", 2);
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    ///
[478](https://docs.rs#478)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_mut(&"apple"), None);
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_mut(&"banana"), Some(&mut 6));
[480](https://docs.rs#480)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_mut(&"pear"), Some(&mut 2));
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    /// ```
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    pub fn get_mut<'a, Q>(&'a mut self, k: &Q) -> Option<&'a mut V>
[483](https://docs.rs#483)    where
[484](https://docs.rs#484)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[485](https://docs.rs#485)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    {
[487](https://docs.rs#487)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[488](https://docs.rs#488)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[489](https://docs.rs#489)
[490](https://docs.rs#490)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[491](https://docs.rs#491)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[492](https://docs.rs#492)
[493](https://docs.rs#493)            Some(unsafe { &mut *(*node_ptr).val.as_mut_ptr() })
[494](https://docs.rs#494)        } else {
[495](https://docs.rs#495)            None
[496](https://docs.rs#496)        }
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    }

[579](https://docs.rs#579)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is

[601](https://docs.rs#601)    pub fn get_or_insert<F>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> &V

[604](https://docs.rs#604)    {

[607](https://docs.rs#607)
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used by passing
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    /// a reference to the key to populate the list and a reference is returned.
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    ///
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    /// # Example
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    ///
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    /// ```
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    ///
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    /// cache.put("One", 1);
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    /// cache.put("Two", 2);
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    /// cache.put("Two", 3);
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    /// cache.put("Three", 4);
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    ///
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("Two", |_|1), &3);
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("Three", |k|k.len()), &4);
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("One", |_|1), &1);
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("One", |k|k.len()), &1);
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    /// ```
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    pub fn get_or_insert_with_key<F>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> &V
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    where
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        F: FnOnce(&K) -> V,
[633](https://docs.rs#633)    {
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(&KeyRef { k: &k }) {
[635](https://docs.rs#635)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[636](https://docs.rs#636)
[637](https://docs.rs#637)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[638](https://docs.rs#638)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[639](https://docs.rs#639)
[640](https://docs.rs#640)            unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() }
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        } else {
[642](https://docs.rs#642)            let v = f(&k);
[643](https://docs.rs#643)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k, v);
[644](https://docs.rs#644)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[645](https://docs.rs#645)
[646](https://docs.rs#646)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[647](https://docs.rs#647)
[648](https://docs.rs#648)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[649](https://docs.rs#649)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[650](https://docs.rs#650)            unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() }
[651](https://docs.rs#651)        }
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    }
[653](https://docs.rs#653)
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used to populate
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    /// the list and a reference is returned. The value referenced by the
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    /// key is only cloned (using `to_owned()`) if it doesn't exist in the
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    /// cache.
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    ///
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    /// # Example
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    ///
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    /// ```
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    /// use std::rc::Rc;
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    ///
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    /// let key1 = Rc::new("1".to_owned());
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    /// let key2 = Rc::new("2".to_owned());
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::<Rc<String>, String>::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key1, ||"One".to_owned()), "One");
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key2, ||"Two".to_owned()), "Two");
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key2, ||"Not two".to_owned()), "Two");
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key2, ||"Again not two".to_owned()), "Two");
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    /// assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key1), 2);
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    /// assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key2), 2); // key2 was only cloned once even though we
[677](https://docs.rs#677)    ///                                         // queried it 3 times
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    /// ```
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    pub fn get_or_insert_ref<'a, Q, F>(&'a mut self, k: &'_ Q, f: F) -> &'a V
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    where
[681](https://docs.rs#681)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[682](https://docs.rs#682)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized + alloc::borrow::ToOwned<Owned = K>,
[683](https://docs.rs#683)        F: FnOnce() -> V,
[684](https://docs.rs#684)    {
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[686](https://docs.rs#686)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[687](https://docs.rs#687)
[688](https://docs.rs#688)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[689](https://docs.rs#689)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[690](https://docs.rs#690)
[691](https://docs.rs#691)            unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() }
[692](https://docs.rs#692)        } else {
[693](https://docs.rs#693)            let v = f();
[694](https://docs.rs#694)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k.to_owned(), v);
[695](https://docs.rs#695)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[696](https://docs.rs#696)
[697](https://docs.rs#697)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[698](https://docs.rs#698)
[699](https://docs.rs#699)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[700](https://docs.rs#700)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[701](https://docs.rs#701)            unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() }
[702](https://docs.rs#702)        }
[703](https://docs.rs#703)    }
[704](https://docs.rs#704)
[705](https://docs.rs#705)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[706](https://docs.rs#706)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[707](https://docs.rs#707)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used to populate
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    /// the list and a reference is returned. If `FnOnce` returns `Err`,
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    /// returns the `Err`.
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    ///

[732](https://docs.rs#732)    pub fn try_get_or_insert<F, E>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> Result<&V, E>

[739](https://docs.rs#739)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[740](https://docs.rs#740)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used by passing
[742](https://docs.rs#742)    /// a reference to the key to populate the list and a reference is returned.
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    /// If `FnOnce` returns `Err`, returns the `Err`.
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    ///
[745](https://docs.rs#745)    /// # Example
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    ///
[747](https://docs.rs#747)    /// ```

[751](https://docs.rs#751)    ///

[753](https://docs.rs#753)    /// cache.put("Two", 2);
[754](https://docs.rs#754)    /// cache.put("Two", 3);
[755](https://docs.rs#755)    /// cache.put("Three", 4);
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    ///
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    /// let f = |_: &&str|->Result<usize, String> {Err("failed".to_owned())};
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    /// let len = |k: &&str|->Result<usize, String> {Ok(k.len())};

[760](https://docs.rs#760)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_with_key("Two", len), Ok(&3));
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_with_key("Three", len), Ok(&4));
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_with_key("Four", f), Err("failed".to_owned()));
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_with_key("Five", len), Ok(&4));
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_with_key("Five", zero), Ok(&4));
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    /// ```
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    pub fn try_get_or_insert_with_key<F, E>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> Result<&V, E>
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    where
[768](https://docs.rs#768)        F: FnOnce(&K) -> Result<V, E>,
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    {
[770](https://docs.rs#770)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(&KeyRef { k: &k }) {
[771](https://docs.rs#771)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[772](https://docs.rs#772)
[773](https://docs.rs#773)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[774](https://docs.rs#774)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[775](https://docs.rs#775)
[776](https://docs.rs#776)            unsafe { Ok(&*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr()) }
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        } else {
[778](https://docs.rs#778)            let v = f(&k)?;
[779](https://docs.rs#779)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k, v);
[780](https://docs.rs#780)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[781](https://docs.rs#781)
[782](https://docs.rs#782)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[783](https://docs.rs#783)
[784](https://docs.rs#784)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[785](https://docs.rs#785)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[786](https://docs.rs#786)            Ok(unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() })
[787](https://docs.rs#787)        }
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    }

[790](https://docs.rs#790)    /// Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
[792](https://docs.rs#792)    /// If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used to populate
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    /// the list and a reference is returned. If `FnOnce` returns `Err`,
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    /// returns the `Err`. The value referenced by the key is only cloned
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    /// (using `to_owned()`) if it doesn't exist in the cache and `FnOnce`
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    /// succeeds.
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    ///
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    /// # Example
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    ///
[800](https://docs.rs#800)    /// ```
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[802](https://docs.rs#802)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    /// use std::rc::Rc;
[804](https://docs.rs#804)    ///
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    /// let key1 = Rc::new("1".to_owned());
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    /// let key2 = Rc::new("2".to_owned());
[807](https://docs.rs#807)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::<Rc<String>, String>::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[808](https://docs.rs#808)    /// let f = ||->Result<String, ()> {Err(())};
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    /// let a = ||->Result<String, ()> {Ok("One".to_owned())};
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    /// let b = ||->Result<String, ()> {Ok("Two".to_owned())};
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_ref(&key1, a), Ok(&"One".to_owned()));
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_ref(&key2, f), Err(()));
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_ref(&key2, b), Ok(&"Two".to_owned()));
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    /// assert_eq!(cache.try_get_or_insert_ref(&key2, a), Ok(&"Two".to_owned()));
[815](https://docs.rs#815)    /// assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key1), 2);
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    /// assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key2), 2); // key2 was only cloned once even though we
[817](https://docs.rs#817)    ///                                         // queried it 3 times
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    /// ```
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    pub fn try_get_or_insert_ref<'a, Q, F, E>(&'a mut self, k: &'_ Q, f: F) -> Result<&'a V, E>
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    where
[821](https://docs.rs#821)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[822](https://docs.rs#822)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized + alloc::borrow::ToOwned<Owned = K>,
[823](https://docs.rs#823)        F: FnOnce() -> Result<V, E>,
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    {
[825](https://docs.rs#825)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[826](https://docs.rs#826)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[827](https://docs.rs#827)
[828](https://docs.rs#828)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[829](https://docs.rs#829)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[830](https://docs.rs#830)
[831](https://docs.rs#831)            unsafe { Ok(&*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr()) }
[832](https://docs.rs#832)        } else {
[833](https://docs.rs#833)            let v = f()?;
[834](https://docs.rs#834)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k.to_owned(), v);
[835](https://docs.rs#835)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[836](https://docs.rs#836)
[837](https://docs.rs#837)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[838](https://docs.rs#838)
[839](https://docs.rs#839)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[840](https://docs.rs#840)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[841](https://docs.rs#841)            Ok(unsafe { &*(*node_ptr).val.as_ptr() })
[842](https://docs.rs#842)        }
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    }

[845](https://docs.rs#845)    /// Returns a mutable reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
[846](https://docs.rs#846)    /// present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.

[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)    {
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)            unsafe { Ok(&mut *(*node_ptr).val.as_mut_ptr()) }
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)        } else {
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)            let v = f()?;
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)            let (_, node) = self.replace_or_create_node(k.to_owned(), v);
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)            let keyref = unsafe { (*node_ptr).key.as_ptr() };
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)            self.map.insert(KeyRef { k: keyref }, node);
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)            unsafe { Ok(&mut *(*node_ptr).val.as_mut_ptr()) }
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)        }
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)    }

[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)        match self.map.remove(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {

[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)                unsafe { Some(val.assume_init()) }

[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)    /// Marks the key as the most recently used one. Returns true if the key
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)    /// was promoted because it exists in the cache, false otherwise.
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)    ///
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)    /// # Example
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)    ///
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)    /// ```
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(3).unwrap());
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)    ///
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)    /// cache.put(1, "a");
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)    /// cache.put(2, "b");
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)    /// cache.put(3, "c");
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)    /// cache.get(&1);
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)    /// cache.get(&2);
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)    ///
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)    /// // If we do `pop_lru` now, we would pop 3.
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)    /// // assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((3, "c")));
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)    ///
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)    /// // By promoting 3, we make sure it isn't popped.
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)    /// assert!(cache.promote(&3));
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)    /// assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((1, "a")));
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)    ///
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)    /// // Promoting an entry that doesn't exist doesn't do anything.
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)    /// assert!(!cache.promote(&4));
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)    /// ```
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)    pub fn promote<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> bool
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)    where
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)    {
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[1428](https://docs.rs#1428)            self.attach(node_ptr);
[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)            true
[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)        } else {
[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)            false
[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)        }
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)    }
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)    /// Marks the key as the least recently used one. Returns true if the key was demoted
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)    /// because it exists in the cache, false otherwise.
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)    ///
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)    /// # Example
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)    ///
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)    /// ```
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(3).unwrap());
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)    ///
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)    /// cache.put(1, "a");
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)    /// cache.put(2, "b");
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)    /// cache.put(3, "c");
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)    /// cache.get(&1);
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)    /// cache.get(&2);
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)    ///
[1451](https://docs.rs#1451)    /// // If we do `pop_lru` now, we would pop 3.
[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)    /// // assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((3, "c")));
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)    ///
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)    /// // By demoting 1 and 2, we make sure those are popped first.
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)    /// assert!(cache.demote(&2));
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)    /// assert!(cache.demote(&1));
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)    /// assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((1, "a")));
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)    /// assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((2, "b")));
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)    ///
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)    /// // Demoting a key that doesn't exist does nothing.
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)    /// assert!(!cache.demote(&4));
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)    /// ```
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)    pub fn demote<Q>(&mut self, k: &Q) -> bool
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)    where
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)        K: Borrow<Q>,
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)    {
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)        if let Some(node) = self.map.get_mut(KeyWrapper::from_ref(k)) {
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = node.as_ptr();
[1470](https://docs.rs#1470)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[1471](https://docs.rs#1471)            self.attach_last(node_ptr);
[1472](https://docs.rs#1472)            true
[1473](https://docs.rs#1473)        } else {
[1474](https://docs.rs#1474)            false
[1475](https://docs.rs#1475)        }
[1476](https://docs.rs#1476)    }
[1477](https://docs.rs#1477)

[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)    /// Resizes the cache. If the new capacity is smaller than the size of the current
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)    /// cache any entries past the new capacity are discarded.
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)    ///
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)    /// # Example
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)    ///
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)    /// ```
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)    /// let mut cache: LruCache<isize, &str> = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)    ///
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)    /// cache.put(1, "a");
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)    /// cache.put(2, "b");
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)    /// cache.resize(NonZeroUsize::new(4).unwrap());
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)    /// cache.put(3, "c");
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)    /// cache.put(4, "d");
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)    ///
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)    /// assert_eq!(cache.len(), 4);
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&1), Some(&"a"));
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&2), Some(&"b"));
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&3), Some(&"c"));
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)    /// assert_eq!(cache.get(&4), Some(&"d"));
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)    /// ```
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)    pub fn resize(&mut self, cap: NonZeroUsize) {
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)        // return early if capacity doesn't change
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)        if cap == self.cap {
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)            return;
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)        }
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)        while self.map.len() > cap.get() {
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)            self.pop_lru();
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)        }
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)        self.map.shrink_to_fit();
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)        self.cap = cap;
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)    }
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)    /// Clears the contents of the cache.

[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)    /// let mut cache: LruCache<isize, &str> = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)    /// assert_eq!(cache.len(), 0);
[1577](https://docs.rs#1577)    ///
[1578](https://docs.rs#1578)    /// cache.put(1, "a");
[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)    /// assert_eq!(cache.len(), 1);

[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)        while self.pop_lru().is_some() {}
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)    }

[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)    /// An iterator visiting all entries in most-recently used order. The iterator element type is

[1606](https://docs.rs#1606)    ///     println!("key: {} val: {}", key, val);
[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)    /// }

[1609](https://docs.rs#1609)    pub fn iter(&self) -> Iter<'_, K, V> {
[1610](https://docs.rs#1610)        Iter {
[1611](https://docs.rs#1611)            len: self.len(),
[1612](https://docs.rs#1612)            ptr: unsafe { (*self.head).next },
[1613](https://docs.rs#1613)            end: unsafe { (*self.tail).prev },
[1614](https://docs.rs#1614)            phantom: PhantomData,
[1615](https://docs.rs#1615)        }
[1616](https://docs.rs#1616)    }
[1617](https://docs.rs#1617)
[1618](https://docs.rs#1618)    /// An iterator visiting all entries in most-recently-used order, giving a mutable reference on
[1619](https://docs.rs#1619)    /// V.  The iterator element type is `(&K, &mut V)`.
[1620](https://docs.rs#1620)    ///
[1621](https://docs.rs#1621)    /// # Examples
[1622](https://docs.rs#1622)    ///
[1623](https://docs.rs#1623)    /// ```
[1624](https://docs.rs#1624)    /// use lru::LruCache;
[1625](https://docs.rs#1625)    /// use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
[1626](https://docs.rs#1626)    ///
[1627](https://docs.rs#1627)    /// struct HddBlock {
[1628](https://docs.rs#1628)    ///     dirty: bool,
[1629](https://docs.rs#1629)    ///     data: [u8; 512]
[1630](https://docs.rs#1630)    /// }
[1631](https://docs.rs#1631)    ///
[1632](https://docs.rs#1632)    /// let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(3).unwrap());
[1633](https://docs.rs#1633)    /// cache.put(0, HddBlock { dirty: false, data: [0x00; 512]});
[1634](https://docs.rs#1634)    /// cache.put(1, HddBlock { dirty: true,  data: [0x55; 512]});
[1635](https://docs.rs#1635)    /// cache.put(2, HddBlock { dirty: true,  data: [0x77; 512]});
[1636](https://docs.rs#1636)    ///
[1637](https://docs.rs#1637)    /// // write dirty blocks to disk.
[1638](https://docs.rs#1638)    /// for (block_id, block) in cache.iter_mut() {
[1639](https://docs.rs#1639)    ///     if block.dirty {
[1640](https://docs.rs#1640)    ///         // write block to disk
[1641](https://docs.rs#1641)    ///         block.dirty = false
[1642](https://docs.rs#1642)    ///     }
[1643](https://docs.rs#1643)    /// }
[1644](https://docs.rs#1644)    /// ```
[1645](https://docs.rs#1645)    pub fn iter_mut(&mut self) -> IterMut<'_, K, V> {
[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)        IterMut {
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)            len: self.len(),
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)            ptr: unsafe { (*self.head).next },
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)            end: unsafe { (*self.tail).prev },
[1650](https://docs.rs#1650)            phantom: PhantomData,
[1651](https://docs.rs#1651)        }
[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)    }
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)    fn remove_first(&mut self) -> Option<Box<LruEntry<K, V>>> {
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)        let next;
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)        unsafe { next = (*self.head).next }
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)        if !core::ptr::eq(next, self.tail) {
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)            let old_key = KeyRef {
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)                k: unsafe { &(*(*(*self.head).next).key.as_ptr()) },
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)            };
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)            let old_node = self.map.remove(&old_key).unwrap();
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = old_node.as_ptr();
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)            unsafe { Some(Box::from_raw(node_ptr)) }
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)        } else {
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)            None
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)        }
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)    }
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)    fn remove_last(&mut self) -> Option<Box<LruEntry<K, V>>> {
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)        let prev;
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)        unsafe { prev = (*self.tail).prev }
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)        if !core::ptr::eq(prev, self.head) {
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)            let old_key = KeyRef {
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)                k: unsafe { &(*(*(*self.tail).prev).key.as_ptr()) },
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)            };
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)            let old_node = self.map.remove(&old_key).unwrap();
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)            let node_ptr: *mut LruEntry<K, V> = old_node.as_ptr();
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)            self.detach(node_ptr);
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)            unsafe { Some(Box::from_raw(node_ptr)) }
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)        } else {
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)            None
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)        }
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)    }
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)    fn detach(&mut self, node: *mut LruEntry<K, V>) {
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)        unsafe {
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)            (*(*node).prev).next = (*node).next;
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)            (*(*node).next).prev = (*node).prev;
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)        }
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)    }
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)    // Attaches `node` after the sigil `self.head` node.
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)    fn attach(&mut self, node: *mut LruEntry<K, V>) {
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)        unsafe {
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)            (*node).next = (*self.head).next;
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)            (*node).prev = self.head;
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)            (*self.head).next = node;
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)            (*(*node).next).prev = node;
[1700](https://docs.rs#1700)        }
[1701](https://docs.rs#1701)    }
[1702](https://docs.rs#1702)
[1703](https://docs.rs#1703)    // Attaches `node` before the sigil `self.tail` node.
[1704](https://docs.rs#1704)    fn attach_last(&mut self, node: *mut LruEntry<K, V>) {
[1705](https://docs.rs#1705)        unsafe {
[1706](https://docs.rs#1706)            (*node).next = self.tail;
[1707](https://docs.rs#1707)            (*node).prev = (*self.tail).prev;
[1708](https://docs.rs#1708)            (*self.tail).prev = node;
[1709](https://docs.rs#1709)            (*(*node).prev).next = node;
[1710](https://docs.rs#1710)        }
[1711](https://docs.rs#1711)    }
[1712](https://docs.rs#1712)}
[1713](https://docs.rs#1713)
[1714](https://docs.rs#1714)impl<K, V, S> Drop for LruCache<K, V, S> {
[1715](https://docs.rs#1715)    fn drop(&mut self) {
[1716](https://docs.rs#1716)        self.map.drain().for_each(|(_, node)| unsafe {
[1717](https://docs.rs#1717)            let mut node = *Box::from_raw(node.as_ptr());
[1718](https://docs.rs#1718)            ptr::drop_in_place((node).key.as_mut_ptr());
[1719](https://docs.rs#1719)            ptr::drop_in_place((node).val.as_mut_ptr());
[1720](https://docs.rs#1720)        });
[1721](https://docs.rs#1721)        // We rebox the head/tail, and because these are maybe-uninit
[1722](https://docs.rs#1722)        // they do not have the absent k/v dropped.
[1723](https://docs.rs#1723)
[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)        let _head = unsafe { *Box::from_raw(self.head) };
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)        let _tail = unsafe { *Box::from_raw(self.tail) };
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)    }
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)}

[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)/// An iterator over the entries of a `LruCache`.

[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)/// This `struct` is created by the [`iter`] method on [`LruCache`][`LruCache`]. See its

[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)/// [`LruCache`]: struct.LruCache.html
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)pub struct Iter<'a, K: 'a, V: 'a> {
[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)    len: usize,
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)    ptr: *const LruEntry<K, V>,
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)    end: *const LruEntry<K, V>,
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)    phantom: PhantomData<&'a K>,
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)}
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)impl<'a, K, V> Iterator for Iter<'a, K, V> {
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)    type Item = (&'a K, &'a V);
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<(&'a K, &'a V)> {
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)        if self.len == 0 {
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)            return None;
[1784](https://docs.rs#1784)        }
[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)        let key = unsafe { &(*(*self.ptr).key.as_ptr()) as &K };
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)        let val = unsafe { &(*(*self.ptr).val.as_ptr()) as &V };
[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)
[1789](https://docs.rs#1789)        self.len -= 1;
[1790](https://docs.rs#1790)        self.ptr = unsafe { (*self.ptr).next };
[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)        Some((key, val))
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)    }
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)    fn size_hint(&self) -> (usize, Option<usize>) {
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)        (self.len, Some(self.len))
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)    }
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)    fn count(self) -> usize {
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)        self.len
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)    }
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)}

[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)    fn next_back(&mut self) -> Option<(&'a K, &'a V)> {
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)        if self.len == 0 {
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)            return None;
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)        }
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)        let key = unsafe { &(*(*self.end).key.as_ptr()) as &K };
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)        let val = unsafe { &(*(*self.end).val.as_ptr()) as &V };
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)

[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)        self.end = unsafe { (*self.end).prev };

[2338](https://docs.rs#2338)    fn test_put_removes_oldest() {
[2339](https://docs.rs#2339)        let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
[2340](https://docs.rs#2340)
[2341](https://docs.rs#2341)        assert_eq!(cache.put("apple", "red"), None);
[2342](https://docs.rs#2342)        assert_eq!(cache.put("banana", "yellow"), None);
[2343](https://docs.rs#2343)        assert_eq!(cache.put("pear", "green"), None);
[2344](https://docs.rs#2344)
[2345](https://docs.rs#2345)        assert!(cache.get(&"apple").is_none());
[2346](https://docs.rs#2346)        assert_opt_eq(cache.get(&"banana"), "yellow");
[2347](https://docs.rs#2347)        assert_opt_eq(cache.get(&"pear"), "green");
[2348](https://docs.rs#2348)
[2349](https://docs.rs#2349)        // Even though we inserted "apple" into the cache earlier it has since been removed from
[2350](https://docs.rs#2350)        // the cache so there is no current value for `put` to return.
[2351](https://docs.rs#2351)        assert_eq!(cache.put("apple", "green"), None);
[2352](https://docs.rs#2352)        assert_eq!(cache.put("tomato", "red"), None);
[2353](https://docs.rs#2353)
[2354](https://docs.rs#2354)        assert!(cache.get(&"pear").is_none());
[2355](https://docs.rs#2355)        assert_opt_eq(cache.get(&"apple"), "green");
[2356](https://docs.rs#2356)        assert_opt_eq(cache.get(&"tomato"), "red");
[2357](https://docs.rs#2357)    }

[2511](https://docs.rs#2511)        for i in 0..75 {

[2513](https://docs.rs#2513)        }
[2514](https://docs.rs#2514)        assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((25, "A")));
[2515](https://docs.rs#2515)        for _ in 0..50 {
[2516](https://docs.rs#2516)            assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), None);
[2517](https://docs.rs#2517)        }
[2518](https://docs.rs#2518)    }

[2876](https://docs.rs#2876)    fn test_no_memory_leaks() {
[2877](https://docs.rs#2877)        static DROP_COUNT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
[2878](https://docs.rs#2878)
[2879](https://docs.rs#2879)        struct DropCounter;
[2880](https://docs.rs#2880)
[2881](https://docs.rs#2881)        impl Drop for DropCounter {
[2882](https://docs.rs#2882)            fn drop(&mut self) {
[2883](https://docs.rs#2883)                DROP_COUNT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[2884](https://docs.rs#2884)            }
[2885](https://docs.rs#2885)        }
[2886](https://docs.rs#2886)
[2887](https://docs.rs#2887)        let n = 100;
[2888](https://docs.rs#2888)        for _ in 0..n {
[2889](https://docs.rs#2889)            let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(1).unwrap());
[2890](https://docs.rs#2890)            for i in 0..n {
[2891](https://docs.rs#2891)                cache.put(i, DropCounter {});
[2892](https://docs.rs#2892)            }
[2893](https://docs.rs#2893)        }
[2894](https://docs.rs#2894)        assert_eq!(DROP_COUNT.load(Ordering::SeqCst), n * n);
[2895](https://docs.rs#2895)    }

[2944](https://docs.rs#2944)    fn test_no_memory_leaks_with_pop() {
[2945](https://docs.rs#2945)        static DROP_COUNT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
[2946](https://docs.rs#2946)
[2947](https://docs.rs#2947)        #[derive(Hash, Eq)]
[2948](https://docs.rs#2948)        struct KeyDropCounter(usize);
[2949](https://docs.rs#2949)
[2950](https://docs.rs#2950)        impl PartialEq for KeyDropCounter {
[2951](https://docs.rs#2951)            fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
[2952](https://docs.rs#2952)                self.0.eq(&other.0)
[2953](https://docs.rs#2953)            }
[2954](https://docs.rs#2954)        }
[2955](https://docs.rs#2955)
[2956](https://docs.rs#2956)        impl Drop for KeyDropCounter {
[2957](https://docs.rs#2957)            fn drop(&mut self) {
[2958](https://docs.rs#2958)                DROP_COUNT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[2959](https://docs.rs#2959)            }
[2960](https://docs.rs#2960)        }
[2961](https://docs.rs#2961)
[2962](https://docs.rs#2962)        let n = 100;
[2963](https://docs.rs#2963)        for _ in 0..n {
[2964](https://docs.rs#2964)            let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(1).unwrap());
[2965](https://docs.rs#2965)
[2966](https://docs.rs#2966)            for i in 0..100 {
[2967](https://docs.rs#2967)                cache.put(KeyDropCounter(i), i);
[2968](https://docs.rs#2968)                cache.pop(&KeyDropCounter(i));
[2969](https://docs.rs#2969)            }
[2970](https://docs.rs#2970)        }
[2971](https://docs.rs#2971)

[3091](https://docs.rs#3091)/// Doctests for what should *not* compile
[3092](https://docs.rs#3092)///

Creates a new LRU Cache that never automatically evicts items and uses the provided hash builder to hash keys.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

```

Puts a key-value pair into cache. If the key already exists in the cache, then it updates
the key’s value and returns the old value. Otherwise, `None` is returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-4)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
assert_eq!(None, cache.put(1, "a"));
assert_eq!(None, cache.put(2, "b"));
assert_eq!(Some("b"), cache.put(2, "beta"));
assert_eq!(cache.get(&1), Some(&"a"));
assert_eq!(cache.get(&2), Some(&"beta"));
```
Pushes a key-value pair into the cache. If an entry with key `k` already exists in
the cache or another cache entry is removed (due to the lru’s capacity),
then it returns the old entry’s key-value pair. Otherwise, returns `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-5)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
assert_eq!(None, cache.push(1, "a"));
assert_eq!(None, cache.push(2, "b"));
// This push call returns (2, "b") because that was previously 2's entry in the cache.
assert_eq!(Some((2, "b")), cache.push(2, "beta"));
// This push call returns (1, "a") because the cache is at capacity and 1's entry was the lru entry.
assert_eq!(Some((1, "a")), cache.push(3, "alpha"));
assert_eq!(cache.get(&1), None);
assert_eq!(cache.get(&2), Some(&"beta"));
assert_eq!(cache.get(&3), Some(&"alpha"));
```
Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache or `None` if it is not
present in the cache. Moves the key to the head of the LRU list if it exists.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-6)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
cache.put(1, "a");
cache.put(2, "b");
cache.put(2, "c");
cache.put(3, "d");
assert_eq!(cache.get(&1), None);
assert_eq!(cache.get(&2), Some(&"c"));
assert_eq!(cache.get(&3), Some(&"d"));
```
Returns a mutable reference to the value of the key in the cache or `None` if it
is not present in the cache. Moves the key to the head of the LRU list if it exists.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-7)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
cache.put("apple", 8);
cache.put("banana", 4);
cache.put("banana", 6);
cache.put("pear", 2);
assert_eq!(cache.get_mut(&"apple"), None);
assert_eq!(cache.get_mut(&"banana"), Some(&mut 6));
assert_eq!(cache.get_mut(&"pear"), Some(&mut 2));
```
Returns a key-value references pair of the key in the cache or `None` if it is not
present in the cache. Moves the key to the head of the LRU list if it exists.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-8)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
cache.put(String::from("1"), "a");
cache.put(String::from("2"), "b");
cache.put(String::from("2"), "c");
cache.put(String::from("3"), "d");
assert_eq!(cache.get_key_value("1"), None);
assert_eq!(cache.get_key_value("2"), Some((&String::from("2"), &"c")));
assert_eq!(cache.get_key_value("3"), Some((&String::from("3"), &"d")));
```
Returns a key-value references pair of the key in the cache or `None` if it is not
present in the cache. The reference to the value of the key is mutable. Moves the key to
the head of the LRU list if it exists.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-9)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
cache.put(1, "a");
cache.put(2, "b");
let (k, v) = cache.get_key_value_mut(&1).unwrap();
assert_eq!(k, &1);
assert_eq!(v, &mut "a");
*v = "aa";
cache.put(3, "c");
assert_eq!(cache.get_key_value(&2), None);
assert_eq!(cache.get_key_value(&1), Some((&1, &"aa")));
assert_eq!(cache.get_key_value(&3), Some((&3, &"c")));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lru/lib.rs.html#601-606)#### pub fn [get_or_insert](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert)<F>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> [&V](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lru/lib.rs.html#601-606)

#### pub fn [get_or_insert](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert)<F>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> [&V](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html)

Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used to populate
the list and a reference is returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-10)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
cache.put(1, "a");
cache.put(2, "b");
cache.put(2, "c");
cache.put(3, "d");
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert(2, ||"a"), &"c");
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert(3, ||"a"), &"d");
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert(1, ||"a"), &"a");
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert(1, ||"b"), &"a");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lru/lib.rs.html#630-652)#### pub fn [get_or_insert_with_key](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_with_key)<F>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> [&V](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html)

#### pub fn [get_or_insert_with_key](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_with_key)<F>(&mut self, k: K, f: F) -> [&V](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html)

Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used by passing
a reference to the key to populate the list and a reference is returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-11)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;

let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
cache.put("One", 1);
cache.put("Two", 2);

cache.put("Three", 4);
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("Two", |_|1), &3);
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("Three", |k|k.len()), &4);
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("One", |_|1), &1);
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_with_key("One", |k|k.len()), &1);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lru/lib.rs.html#679-703)#### pub fn [get_or_insert_ref](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_ref)<'a, Q, F>(&'a mut self, k: [&Q](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html), f: F) -> [&'a V](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lru/lib.rs.html#679-703)

#### pub fn [get_or_insert_ref](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_ref)<'a, Q, F>(&'a mut self, k: [&Q](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html), f: F) -> [&'a V](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html)

Returns a reference to the value of the key in the cache if it is
present in the cache and moves the key to the head of the LRU list.
If the key does not exist the provided `FnOnce` is used to populate
the list and a reference is returned. The value referenced by the
key is only cloned (using `to_owned()`) if it doesn’t exist in the
cache.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-12)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
use std::rc::Rc;
let key1 = Rc::new("1".to_owned());
let key2 = Rc::new("2".to_owned());
let mut cache = LruCache::<Rc<String>, String>::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key1, ||"One".to_owned()), "One");
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key2, ||"Two".to_owned()), "Two");
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key2, ||"Not two".to_owned()), "Two");
assert_eq!(cache.get_or_insert_ref(&key2, ||"Again not two".to_owned()), "Two");
assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key1), 2);
assert_eq!(Rc::strong_count(&key2), 2); // key2 was only cloned once even though we
                                        // queried it 3 times
```

Marks the key as the most recently used one. Returns true if the key was promoted because it exists in the cache, false otherwise.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-31)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(3).unwrap());
cache.put(1, "a");
cache.put(2, "b");
cache.put(3, "c");
cache.get(&1);
cache.get(&2);
// If we do `pop_lru` now, we would pop 3.
// assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((3, "c")));
// By promoting 3, we make sure it isn't popped.
assert!(cache.promote(&3));
assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((1, "a")));
// Promoting an entry that doesn't exist doesn't do anything.
assert!(!cache.promote(&4));
```
Marks the key as the least recently used one. Returns true if the key was demoted because it exists in the cache, false otherwise.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-32)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(3).unwrap());
cache.put(1, "a");
cache.put(2, "b");
cache.put(3, "c");
cache.get(&1);
cache.get(&2);
// If we do `pop_lru` now, we would pop 3.
// assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((3, "c")));
// By demoting 1 and 2, we make sure those are popped first.
assert!(cache.demote(&2));
assert!(cache.demote(&1));
assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((1, "a")));
assert_eq!(cache.pop_lru(), Some((2, "b")));
// Demoting a key that doesn't exist does nothing.
assert!(!cache.demote(&4));
```

assert_eq!(cache.len(), 0);
cache.put(1, "a");
assert_eq!(cache.len(), 1);
cache.put(2, "b");
assert_eq!(cache.len(), 2);
cache.put(3, "c");
assert_eq!(cache.len(), 2);
```
Returns a bool indicating whether the cache is empty or not.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-34)Example

```

assert!(!cache.is_empty());
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lru/lib.rs.html#1554-1566)#### pub fn [resize](https://docs.rs#method.resize)(&mut self, cap: [NonZeroUsize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/num/nonzero/type.NonZeroUsize.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lru/lib.rs.html#1554-1566)

#### pub fn [resize](https://docs.rs#method.resize)(&mut self, cap: [NonZeroUsize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/num/nonzero/type.NonZeroUsize.html))

Resizes the cache. If the new capacity is smaller than the size of the current cache any entries past the new capacity are discarded.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-36)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache: LruCache<isize, &str> = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
cache.put(1, "a");
cache.put(2, "b");
cache.resize(NonZeroUsize::new(4).unwrap());
cache.put(3, "c");
cache.put(4, "d");
assert_eq!(cache.len(), 4);
assert_eq!(cache.get(&1), Some(&"a"));
assert_eq!(cache.get(&2), Some(&"b"));
assert_eq!(cache.get(&3), Some(&"c"));
assert_eq!(cache.get(&4), Some(&"d"));
```
Clears the contents of the cache.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-37)Example

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache: LruCache<isize, &str> = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
assert_eq!(cache.len(), 0);
cache.put(1, "a");
assert_eq!(cache.len(), 1);
cache.put(2, "b");
assert_eq!(cache.len(), 2);
cache.clear();
assert_eq!(cache.len(), 0);
```
An iterator visiting all entries in most-recently used order. The iterator element type is
`(&K, &V)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(3).unwrap());
cache.put("a", 1);
cache.put("b", 2);
cache.put("c", 3);
for (key, val) in cache.iter() {
    println!("key: {} val: {}", key, val);
}
```
An iterator visiting all entries in most-recently-used order, giving a mutable reference on
V.  The iterator element type is `(&K, &mut V)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
struct HddBlock {
    dirty: bool,
    data: [u8; 512]
}
let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(3).unwrap());
cache.put(0, HddBlock { dirty: false, data: [0x00; 512]});
cache.put(1, HddBlock { dirty: true,  data: [0x55; 512]});
cache.put(2, HddBlock { dirty: true,  data: [0x77; 512]});
// write dirty blocks to disk.
for (block_id, block) in cache.iter_mut() {
    if block.dirty {
        // write block to disk
        block.dirty = false
    }
}
```

# lru - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lru/0.18.0/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/lru/

## Expand description

An implementation of a LRU cache. The cache supports `get`, `get_mut`, `put`,
and `pop` operations, all of which are O(1). This crate was heavily influenced
by the [LRU Cache implementation in an earlier version of Rust’s std::collections crate](https://doc.rust-lang.org/0.12.0/std/collections/lru_cache/struct.LruCache.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
extern crate lru;
use lru::LruCache;
use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
fn main() {
        let mut cache = LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(2).unwrap());
        cache.put("apple", 3);
        cache.put("banana", 2);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"apple").unwrap(), 3);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 2);
        assert!(cache.get(&"pear").is_none());
        assert_eq!(cache.put("banana", 4), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(cache.put("pear", 5), None);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"pear").unwrap(), 5);
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 4);
        assert!(cache.get(&"apple").is_none());
        {
            let v = cache.get_mut(&"banana").unwrap();
            *v = 6;
        }
        assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"banana").unwrap(), 6);
}
```

[198](https://docs.rs#198)    K: Hash + PartialEq + Eq + Clone,

[202](https://docs.rs#202)    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
[203](https://docs.rs#203)        let map_cap = if self.is_unbounded() {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)            self.len()
[205](https://docs.rs#205)        } else {
[206](https://docs.rs#206)            self.cap().get()
[207](https://docs.rs#207)        };
[208](https://docs.rs#208)        let mut new_lru = LruCache::construct(
[209](https://docs.rs#209)            self.cap(),
[210](https://docs.rs#210)            HashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(map_cap, self.map.hasher().clone()),
[211](https://docs.rs#211)        );
[212](https://docs.rs#212)
[213](https://docs.rs#213)        for (key, value) in self.iter().rev() {
[214](https://docs.rs#214)            new_lru.push(key.clone(), value.clone());
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        }
[216](https://docs.rs#216)
[217](https://docs.rs#217)        new_lru
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    }
